es.text: Un gran escenario se materializa. The Sonnet Man avanza desde un foco dorado, micrófono en mano. Las palabras de Shakespeare se transforman en rimas de hip-hop mientras el público lo aclama.
es.english: A grand stage materializes. The Sonnet Man steps forward from a golden spotlight, microphone in hand. Shakespeare's words transform into hip-hop bars as the crowd cheers.
es.back: A grand stage materializes. The Sonnet Man advances from a golden spotlight, microphone in hand, Shakespeare’s words transformed into hip-hop rhymes as the audience cheers for him.
es.controlEnglish: A moonlit balcony scene unfolds. Romeo reaches upward as Juliet appears above. Rose petals drift through the air. The scene pulses with a warm crimson glow.

es.text: ¿He de compararte con un día de verano?
es.english: Shall I compare thee to a summer's day?
es.back: Should I compare you to a summer day?
es.controlEnglish: Lord, what fools these mortals be!

es.text: Se despliega la escena de un balcón a la luz de la luna. Romeo tiende la mano hacia lo alto mientras Julieta aparece arriba. Pétalos de rosa flotan en el aire. La escena late con un cálido resplandor carmesí.
es.english: A moonlit balcony scene unfolds. Romeo reaches upward as Juliet appears above. Rose petals drift through the air. The scene pulses with a warm crimson glow.
es.back: The scene of a moonlit balcony unfolds. Romeo reaches up as Juliet appears above. Rose petals float in the air. The scene beats with a warm crimson glow.
es.controlEnglish: The Capulet garden blooms in moonlight. Juliet stands among roses, her eyes bright with defiance. A nightingale sings from the branches above.

es.text: El jardín de los Capuleto florece a la luz de la luna. Julieta está entre las rosas, con los ojos brillantes de desafío. Un ruiseñor canta desde las ramas.
es.english: The Capulet garden blooms in moonlight. Juliet stands among roses, her eyes bright with defiance. A nightingale sings from the branches above.
es.back: The garden of the Capulets blooms in the moonlight. Juliet is among the roses, her eyes shining with defiance, and a nightingale sings from the branches.
es.controlEnglish: The castle of Elsinore emerges from shadow. Hamlet stands at the battlements, Yorick's skull hovering beside him. A spectral figure appears on the ramparts above.

es.text: El castillo de Elsinor emerge de la sombra. Hamlet está en las almenas, con la calavera de Yorick flotando a su lado. Una figura espectral aparece en lo alto de la muralla.
es.english: The castle of Elsinore emerges from shadow. Hamlet stands at the battlements, Yorick's skull hovering beside him. A spectral figure appears on the ramparts above.
es.back: The castle of Elsinore emerges from the shadows. Hamlet is on the crenellations, with Yorick's skull floating beside him, and a spectral figure appears at the top of the wall.
es.controlEnglish: A gentle stream winds through a willow grove. Ophelia floats among wildflowers, whispering forgotten verses. Petals circle in the current.

es.text: Un arroyo manso serpentea por un bosque de sauces. Ofelia flota entre flores silvestres, susurrando versos olvidados. Los pétalos giran en la corriente.
es.english: A gentle stream winds through a willow grove. Ophelia floats among wildflowers, whispering forgotten verses. Petals circle in the current.
es.back: A gentle stream meanders through a willow forest. Ophelia floats among wild flowers, whispering forgotten verses, the petals spin in the stream.
es.controlEnglish: A Verona street erupts in chaos. Mercutio dances between blades, laughing in the face of danger. Sparks fly from clashing steel.

es.text: Una calle de Verona estalla en caos. Mercucio baila entre las espadas, riéndose del peligro. Saltan chispas del acero que choca.
es.english: A Verona street erupts in chaos. Mercutio dances between blades, laughing in the face of danger. Sparks fly from clashing steel.
es.back: A street in Verona bursts into chaos. Mercutio dances between the swords, laughing at the danger; sparks spring from the colliding steel.
es.controlEnglish: The enchanted forest shimmers with mischief. Puck darts between ancient oaks, leaving trails of pixie dust. Sleeping mortals dream strange dreams below.

es.text: El bosque encantado reluce de travesura. Puck se escurre entre robles antiguos, dejando estelas de polvo de hadas. Abajo, los mortales dormidos sueñan sueños extraños.
es.english: The enchanted forest shimmers with mischief. Puck darts between ancient oaks, leaving trails of pixie dust. Sleeping mortals dream strange dreams below.
es.back: The enchanted forest shines with mischief. Puck slips through ancient oaks, leaving trails of fairy dust behind him, and below, asleep mortals dream strange dreams.
es.controlEnglish: A throne of living vines rises from the forest floor. Titania commands her fairy court as fireflies illuminate the canopy. Nature itself bows to her will.

es.text: ¡Señor, qué necios son estos mortales!
es.english: Lord, what fools these mortals be!
es.back: Lord, how foolish these mortals are!
es.controlEnglish: Come, sit thee down upon this flowery bed.

es.text: Un trono de enredaderas vivas se alza del suelo del bosque. Titania gobierna su corte de hadas mientras las luciérnagas iluminan la fronda. La naturaleza misma se inclina ante su voluntad.
es.english: A throne of living vines rises from the forest floor. Titania commands her fairy court as fireflies illuminate the canopy. Nature itself bows to her will.
es.back: A throne of living vines rises from the forest floor. Titania rules her fairy court as fireflies illuminate the foliage, and nature itself bows to her will.
es.controlEnglish: A skull rests on velvet in a dim crypt. Ghostly laughter echoes as memories of the court jester flicker like candlelight.

es.text: Ven, siéntate en este lecho florido.
es.english: Come, sit thee down upon this flowery bed.
es.back: Come, sit on this flowery bed.
es.controlEnglish: Now my charms are all o'erthrown.

es.text: Una calavera reposa sobre terciopelo en una cripta en penumbra. Resuena una risa fantasmal mientras los recuerdos del bufón de la corte tiemblan como la luz de una vela.
es.english: A skull rests on velvet in a dim crypt. Ghostly laughter echoes as memories of the court jester flicker like candlelight.
es.back: A skull rests on velvet in a darkened crypt, ghostly laughter resounds as the memories of the court buffoon tremble like candlelight.
es.controlEnglish: A gnarled staff crackles with arcane energy. The tempest swirls around it as Prospero whispers his final spell. Lightning splits the sky.

es.text: La calavera de Yorick
es.english: Yorick's Skull
es.back: The Skull of Yorick
es.controlEnglish: Prospero's Staff

es.text: Un báculo nudoso chisporrotea de energía arcana. La tempestad gira a su alrededor mientras Próspero susurra su último conjuro. El rayo parte el cielo.
es.english: A gnarled staff crackles with arcane energy. The tempest swirls around it as Prospero whispers his final spell. Lightning splits the sky.
es.back: A knotted staff sparkles with arcane energy. The storm swirls around it as Prospero whispers his last spell, and lightning breaks through the sky.
es.controlEnglish: A glowing vial pulses with rose-colored light. Hearts drift upward from its surface as a sweet melody fills the air.

es.text: Ahora mis hechizos están todos deshechos.
es.english: Now my charms are all o'erthrown.
es.back: Now my spells are all undone.
es.controlEnglish: The course of true love never did run smooth.

es.text: El báculo de Próspero
es.english: Prospero's Staff
es.back: The staff of Prospero
es.controlEnglish: Love Potion

es.text: Un frasco luminoso late con luz rosada. De su superficie suben corazones mientras una dulce melodía llena el aire.
es.english: A glowing vial pulses with rose-colored light. Hearts drift upward from its surface as a sweet melody fills the air.
es.back: A luminous jar beats with pink light, hearts rise from its surface as a sweet melody fills the air.
es.controlEnglish: A bubbling cauldron belches green smoke. Three shadowy figures circle it, chanting. Eyes glow from the dark woods beyond.

es.text: El curso del amor verdadero nunca fue sereno.
es.english: The course of true love never did run smooth.
es.back: The course of true love was never serene.
es.controlEnglish: I am the drudge and toil in your delight.

es.text: Filtro de amor
es.english: Love Potion
es.back: Filter of love
es.controlEnglish: Witches' Brew

es.text: Un caldero burbujeante escupe humo verde. Tres figuras sombrías lo rodean, salmodiando. Unos ojos brillan desde el bosque oscuro.
es.english: A bubbling cauldron belches green smoke. Three shadowy figures circle it, chanting. Eyes glow from the dark woods beyond.
es.back: A bubbling cauldron spews green smoke. Three shadowy figures surround it, singing hymns, and eyes shine from the dark forest.
es.controlEnglish: The Prince stands on the steps of Verona's palace, his voice commanding silence over the feuding crowd. A golden scepter burns with authority.

es.text: Brebaje de las brujas
es.english: Witches' Brew
es.back: Brew of the witches
es.controlEnglish: Dagger of the Mind

es.text: El Príncipe está en la escalinata del palacio de Verona; su voz impone silencio a la multitud enfrentada. Un cetro dorado arde de autoridad.
es.english: The Prince stands on the steps of Verona's palace, his voice commanding silence over the feuding crowd. A golden scepter burns with authority.
es.back: The Prince stands on the steps of the palace of Verona; his voice silenced the crowd, and a golden scepter burned with authority.
es.controlEnglish: A candlelit cell in a monastery. The Friar tends his garden of herbs and poisons, wisdom etched into his weathered face.

es.text: Una celda de monasterio a la luz de las velas. El fraile cuida su huerto de hierbas y venenos, con la sabiduría grabada en el rostro curtido.
es.english: A candlelit cell in a monastery. The Friar tends his garden of herbs and poisons, wisdom etched into his weathered face.
es.back: A monastery cell in candlelight, the friar cares for his garden of herbs and poisons, with wisdom engraved on his tanned face.
es.controlEnglish: A warm kitchen in the Capulet house. The Nurse bustles with fierce devotion, a secret letter tucked in her apron.

es.text: Una cocina cálida en casa de los Capuleto. El ama trajina con feroz devoción, con una carta secreta guardada en el delantal.
es.english: A warm kitchen in the Capulet house. The Nurse bustles with fierce devotion, a secret letter tucked in her apron.
es.back: A warm kitchen in the house of the Capulets, where the caretaker treats Trajana with ferocious devotion, keeping a secret letter in his apron.
es.controlEnglish: An island shrouded in tempest. Prospero raises his hands as lightning obeys his will, the sea churning at his command.

es.text: Yo soy la esclava que se afana por tu deleite.
es.english: I am the drudge and toil in your delight.
es.back: I am the slave who cares for your delight.
es.controlEnglish: We are such stuff as dreams are made on.

es.text: Una isla envuelta en la tempestad. Próspero alza las manos mientras el rayo obedece su voluntad y el mar se agita a su mandato.
es.english: An island shrouded in tempest. Prospero raises his hands as lightning obeys his will, the sea churning at his command.
es.back: An island enveloped in storm, Prospero raises his hands as the lightning obeys his will and the sea stirred at his command.
es.controlEnglish: A shimmering spirit dissolves into wind and light, reforming as music. Ariel dances between the visible and invisible.

es.text: Estamos hechos de la misma materia que los sueños.
es.english: We are such stuff as dreams are made on.
es.back: We are made of the same material as dreams.
es.controlEnglish: All hail, great master! Grave sir, hail!

es.text: Un espíritu tornasolado se disuelve en viento y luz, y vuelve a formarse como música. Ariel danza entre lo visible y lo invisible.
es.english: A shimmering spirit dissolves into wind and light, reforming as music. Ariel dances between the visible and invisible.
es.back: A torn spirit dissolves in wind and light, and re-forms as music.Ariel dances between the visible and the invisible.
es.controlEnglish: A cave mouth on a wild shore. Caliban crouches among the rocks, eyes burning with resentment and primal intelligence.

es.text: ¡Salve, gran amo! ¡Grave señor, salve!
es.english: All hail, great master! Grave sir, hail!
es.back: Hail, great master! Hail, grave lord!
es.controlEnglish: This island's mine, by Sycorax my mother.

es.text: La boca de una cueva en una costa salvaje. Calibán se agazapa entre las rocas, con los ojos ardiendo de rencor y de una inteligencia primitiva.
es.english: A cave mouth on a wild shore. Caliban crouches among the rocks, eyes burning with resentment and primal intelligence.
es.back: The mouth of a cave on a wild coast, Caliban crouches among the rocks, his eyes burning with rancor and primitive intelligence.
es.controlEnglish: A Verona plaza at dawn. Benvolio stands between drawn swords, his open hands the only weapon against the gathering storm.

es.text: Esta isla es mía, por Sycorax, mi madre.
es.english: This island's mine, by Sycorax my mother.
es.back: This island is mine, by Sycorax, my mother.
es.controlEnglish: Ill met by moonlight, proud Titania.

es.text: Una plaza de Verona al amanecer. Benvolio se interpone entre espadas desnudas; sus manos abiertas son la única arma contra la tormenta que se avecina.
es.english: A Verona plaza at dawn. Benvolio stands between drawn swords, his open hands the only weapon against the gathering storm.
es.back: A square in Verona at dawn: Benvolio stands between bare swords; his open hands are the only weapon against the storm that is coming.
es.controlEnglish: A Verona alley ablaze with torchlight. Tybalt draws his rapier with lethal grace, his eyes fixed on his enemy.

es.text: Un callejón de Verona incendiado por las antorchas. Tebaldo desenvaina su estoque con gracia letal, con los ojos clavados en su enemigo.
es.english: A Verona alley ablaze with torchlight. Tybalt draws his rapier with lethal grace, his eyes fixed on his enemy.
es.back: An alley in Verona set on fire by the torches, Tebaldo unfolds his stock with lethal grace, eyes fixed on his enemy.
es.controlEnglish: The throne room of Elsinore, draped in false splendor. Claudius grips the crown, a vial of poison hidden in his robes.

es.text: El salón del trono de Elsinor, revestido de falso esplendor. Claudio aferra la corona, con un frasco de veneno oculto en sus ropas.
es.english: The throne room of Elsinore, draped in false splendor. Claudius grips the crown, a vial of poison hidden in his robes.
es.back: The throne hall of Elsinore, clad in false splendor.Claudius holds the crown, with a vial of poison hidden in his clothes.
es.controlEnglish: A moonlit glade deep in the enchanted forest. Oberon materializes from shadow, his crown of antlers catching silver light.

es.text: Un claro iluminado por la luna en lo hondo del bosque encantado. Oberón surge de la sombra; su corona de astas recoge la luz de plata.
es.english: A moonlit glade deep in the enchanted forest. Oberon materializes from shadow, his crown of antlers catching silver light.
es.back: A moonlit clearing deep in the enchanted forest. Oberon rises from the shadows. His crown of horns catches the silver light.
es.controlEnglish: A spectral dagger floats in darkness, its blade dripping with phantom blood. Macbeth's hand reaches but can never grasp it.

es.text: Mal encuentro a la luz de la luna, orgullosa Titania.
es.english: Ill met by moonlight, proud Titania.
es.back: Bad encounter in the moonlight, proud Titania.
es.controlEnglish: I'll put a girdle round about the earth in forty minutes.

es.text: Una daga espectral flota en la oscuridad, con la hoja goteando sangre fantasma. La mano de Macbeth se alarga, pero nunca logra asirla.
es.english: A spectral dagger floats in darkness, its blade dripping with phantom blood. Macbeth's hand reaches but can never grasp it.
es.back: A spectral dagger floats in the dark, with the blade dripping ghost blood; Macbeth's hand stretches out but never gets hold of it.
es.controlEnglish: A crushed purple flower drips iridescent nectar into a waiting palm. Wherever it falls, eyes change — and hearts follow.

es.text: La daga de la mente
es.english: Dagger of the Mind
es.back: The dagger of the mind
es.controlEnglish: Puck's Flower Juice

es.text: Una flor púrpura aplastada deja caer un néctar irisado en una palma que espera. Allí donde cae, los ojos cambian, y los corazones los siguen.
es.english: A crushed purple flower drips iridescent nectar into a waiting palm. Wherever it falls, eyes change — and hearts follow.
es.back: A crushed purple flower drops iridescent nectar on a waiting palm; where it falls, eyes change, and hearts follow.
es.controlEnglish: A bloodstained throne room in Dunsinane. Macbeth grips his sword with trembling hands, the crown heavy on his brow. Birnam Wood stirs on the distant hill.

es.text: Pondré un cinturón alrededor de la tierra en cuarenta minutos.
es.english: I'll put a girdle round about the earth in forty minutes.
es.back: I will put a belt around the earth in forty minutes.
es.controlEnglish: I am not what I am.

es.text: Jugo de la flor de Puck
es.english: Puck's Flower Juice
es.back: Puck Flower Juice
es.controlEnglish: Lord Montague

es.text: Un salón del trono manchado de sangre en Dunsinane. Macbeth empuña la espada con manos temblorosas; la corona le pesa en la frente. El bosque de Birnam se mueve en la colina lejana.
es.english: A bloodstained throne room in Dunsinane. Macbeth grips his sword with trembling hands, the crown heavy on his brow. Birnam Wood stirs on the distant hill.
es.back: A blood-stained throne hall in Dunsinane. Macbeth holds the sword with trembling hands; the crown weighs on his forehead.The forest of Birnam moves on the distant hill.
es.controlEnglish: A candlelit chamber in the Scottish castle. Lady Macbeth paces the cold stones, wringing phantom bloodstains from her hands. Shadows cling to her like a second skin.

es.text: Una cámara del castillo escocés a la luz de las velas. Lady Macbeth recorre las frías losas, frotándose de las manos manchas de sangre que no existen. Las sombras se le pegan como una segunda piel.
es.english: A candlelit chamber in the Scottish castle. Lady Macbeth paces the cold stones, wringing phantom bloodstains from her hands. Shadows cling to her like a second skin.
es.back: A chamber of the Scottish castle in candlelight. Lady Macbeth walks on the cold slabs, rubbing blood stains from her hands that do not exist.The shadows stick to her like a second skin.
es.controlEnglish: A misty Scottish heath at twilight. Banquo stands resolute as three spectral figures whisper destinies into the wind. His ghost will haunt the living.

es.text: Un páramo escocés brumoso al crepúsculo. Banquo se mantiene firme mientras tres figuras espectrales susurran destinos al viento. Su fantasma perseguirá a los vivos.
es.english: A misty Scottish heath at twilight. Banquo stands resolute as three spectral figures whisper destinies into the wind. His ghost will haunt the living.
es.back: A misty Scottish moor at dusk. Banquo stands firm as three spectral figures whisper destinies to the wind, his ghost haunting the living.
es.controlEnglish: A windswept Illyrian shore. Viola pulls a sailor's cap over her cropped hair, twin identities shimmering in her eyes. The sea whispers secrets of her lost brother.

es.text: Una costa de Iliria azotada por el viento. Viola se cala una gorra de marinero sobre el pelo corto; dos identidades brillan en sus ojos. El mar susurra secretos de su hermano perdido.
es.english: A windswept Illyrian shore. Viola pulls a sailor's cap over her cropped hair, twin identities shimmering in her eyes. The sea whispers secrets of her lost brother.
es.back: A windswept Illyrian coast. Viola puts a sailor’s cap over her short hair; two identities shine in her eyes, the sea whispering secrets of her lost brother.
es.controlEnglish: A sunlit garden in Olivia's estate. Malvolio struts in garish yellow stockings, cross-gartered and grinning, clutching a forged love letter to his chest.

es.text: No soy lo que soy.
es.english: I am not what I am.
es.back: I'm not what I am.
es.controlEnglish: Some are born great, some achieve greatness, and some have greatness thrust upon them.

es.text: Un jardín soleado en la finca de Olivia. Malvolio se pavonea con chillonas medias amarillas y ligas cruzadas, sonriente, apretando contra el pecho una carta de amor falsificada.
es.english: A sunlit garden in Olivia's estate. Malvolio struts in garish yellow stockings, cross-gartered and grinning, clutching a forged love letter to his chest.
es.back: A sunny garden on Olivia’s estate, Malvolio flaunts in yellow squeaky stockings and crossed garters, smiling, pressing against his chest a fake love letter.
es.controlEnglish: A veiled countess in mourning lifts her veil to reveal breathtaking beauty. Olivia's garden blooms with jasmine and lavender as the disguised messenger steals her heart.

es.text: Algunos nacen grandes, algunos alcanzan la grandeza, y a algunos la grandeza les es impuesta.
es.english: Some are born great, some achieve greatness, and some have greatness thrust upon them.
es.back: Some are born great, some attain greatness, and to some greatness is imposed.
es.controlEnglish: Love sought is good, but given unsought, is better.

es.text: Una condesa de luto alza el velo y descubre una belleza que corta el aliento. El jardín de Olivia florece de jazmín y lavanda mientras el mensajero disfrazado le roba el corazón.
es.english: A veiled countess in mourning lifts her veil to reveal breathtaking beauty. Olivia's garden blooms with jasmine and lavender as the disguised messenger steals her heart.
es.back: A mourning countess lifts her veil and discovers a breathtaking beauty: Olivia’s garden blooms with jasmine and lavender as the disguised messenger steals her heart.
es.controlEnglish: The Roman Senate, marble pillars stained crimson. Brutus stands among the conspirators, his blade still trembling. The weight of the republic rests on his bloodied hands.

es.text: El amor buscado es bueno, pero dado sin buscarlo es mejor.
es.english: Love sought is good, but given unsought, is better.
es.back: Love sought is good, but given without seeking it is better.
es.controlEnglish: Marry, that marry is the very theme I came to talk of.

es.text: El Senado romano, con las columnas de mármol teñidas de carmesí. Bruto está entre los conjurados, con la hoja aún temblando. El peso de la república descansa en sus manos ensangrentadas.
es.english: The Roman Senate, marble pillars stained crimson. Brutus stands among the conspirators, his blade still trembling. The weight of the republic rests on his bloodied hands.
es.back: The Roman Senate, with its crimson-tinted marble columns. Brutus is among the conjured, his blade still shaking; the weight of the republic rests on his bloody hands.
es.controlEnglish: A torchlit Roman alley at midnight. Cassius leans close, whispering sedition with a lean and hungry look. Forged letters spill from his toga.

es.text: Un callejón romano a medianoche, a la luz de las antorchas. Casio se acerca y susurra sedición con mirada flaca y hambrienta. De su toga caen cartas falsificadas.
es.english: A torchlit Roman alley at midnight. Cassius leans close, whispering sedition with a lean and hungry look. Forged letters spill from his toga.
es.back: A Roman alley at midnight, in the light of torches. Casio approaches and whispers sedition with a skinny, hungry look; forged letters fall from his toga.
es.controlEnglish: The Roman Forum erupts in fury. Mark Antony holds Caesar's bloodied cloak aloft before the mob, his words turning grief into fire. The republic crumbles with every syllable.

es.text: El Foro romano estalla de furia. Marco Antonio alza ante la turba el manto ensangrentado de César; sus palabras convierten el duelo en fuego. La república se derrumba con cada sílaba.
es.english: The Roman Forum erupts in fury. Mark Antony holds Caesar's bloodied cloak aloft before the mob, his words turning grief into fire. The republic crumbles with every syllable.
es.back: The Roman Forum bursts into fury, Marcus Antonius raises Caesar's bloody cloak before the crowd; his words turn the duel into fire. The republic collapses with every syllable.
es.controlEnglish: The Montague estate at dawn. Lord Montague watches from a high window as his son wanders the misty orchards below, lovesick and unreachable.

es.text: La hacienda de los Montesco al amanecer. El señor Montesco mira desde una ventana alta a su hijo, que vaga por los huertos brumosos, enfermo de amor e inalcanzable.
es.english: The Montague estate at dawn. Lord Montague watches from a high window as his son wanders the misty orchards below, lovesick and unreachable.
es.back: The Montesco estate at dawn: Mr. Montesco looks from a high window at his son, who wanders through the misty gardens, sick of love and unattainable.
es.controlEnglish: The Capulet great hall draped in silk. Lady Capulet arranges her daughter's fate like flowers in a vase, ambition glittering behind every gracious smile.

es.text: Señor Montesco
es.english: Lord Montague
es.back: Mr. Montesco
es.controlEnglish: Lady Capulet

es.text: El gran salón de los Capuleto, vestido de seda. La señora Capuleto dispone el destino de su hija como flores en un jarrón; la ambición brilla tras cada sonrisa amable.
es.english: The Capulet great hall draped in silk. Lady Capulet arranges her daughter's fate like flowers in a vase, ambition glittering behind every gracious smile.
es.back: The great hall of the Capulets, dressed in silk.Lady Capulet arranges her daughter's fate like flowers in a vase; ambition shines behind every kind smile.
es.controlEnglish: The battlements of Elsinore in the cold hour before dawn. Horatio stands vigil beside Hamlet, the one true friend in a court of serpents.

es.text: Casarte, ese es justamente el tema del que venía a hablar.
es.english: Marry, that marry is the very theme I came to talk of.
es.back: Getting married, that is exactly the subject I came to talk about.
es.controlEnglish: I have had a most rare vision. I have had a dream, past the wit of man.

es.text: Señora Capuleto
es.english: Lady Capulet
es.back: Señora Capuleto
es.controlEnglish: Romeo's Ring

es.text: Las almenas de Elsinor en la hora fría que precede al alba. Horacio vela junto a Hamlet, el único amigo verdadero en una corte de serpientes.
es.english: The battlements of Elsinore in the cold hour before dawn. Horatio stands vigil beside Hamlet, the one true friend in a court of serpents.
es.back: The crenellations of Elsinore in the cold hour before dawn, Horatio watches with Hamlet, the only true friend in a court of snakes.
es.controlEnglish: A forest clearing aglow with fairy light. Bottom wears an ass's head with bewildered dignity as Titania drapes him in garlands. The fairies stifle their laughter.

es.text: Un claro del bosque encendido de luz de hadas. Bottom lleva una cabeza de asno con desconcertada dignidad mientras Titania lo cubre de guirnaldas. Las hadas ahogan la risa.
es.english: A forest clearing aglow with fairy light. Bottom wears an ass's head with bewildered dignity as Titania drapes him in garlands. The fairies stifle their laughter.
es.back: A forest clearing lit by fairy light. Bottom carries a donkey's head with baffled dignity as Titania covers it with garlands.
es.controlEnglish: The churchyard of Verona at dusk. Paris lays flowers at Juliet's tomb, unaware of the desperate lover who approaches from the shadows.

es.text: He tenido una visión rarísima. He tenido un sueño que supera el entendimiento del hombre.
es.english: I have had a most rare vision. I have had a dream, past the wit of man.
es.back: I have had a very rare vision, I have had a dream that is beyond the understanding of man.
es.controlEnglish: O brave new world, that has such people in it!

es.text: El cementerio de Verona al anochecer. Paris deja flores en la tumba de Julieta, sin saber del amante desesperado que se acerca desde las sombras.
es.english: The churchyard of Verona at dusk. Paris lays flowers at Juliet's tomb, unaware of the desperate lover who approaches from the shadows.
es.back: Paris leaves flowers on Juliet's grave, unaware of the desperate lover who is approaching from the shadows.
es.controlEnglish: A pristine beach on Prospero's island. Miranda sees the shipwrecked sailors for the first time, her eyes wide with wonder at a world she never knew existed.

es.text: Una playa intacta en la isla de Próspero. Miranda ve por primera vez a los náufragos, con los ojos muy abiertos de asombro ante un mundo que no sabía que existía.
es.english: A pristine beach on Prospero's island. Miranda sees the shipwrecked sailors for the first time, her eyes wide with wonder at a world she never knew existed.
es.back: An intact beach on Prospero's island, Miranda sees the shipwrecked for the first time, with her eyes wide open in amazement at a world she didn't know existed.
es.controlEnglish: A golden ring rests on a stone balcony ledge, catching moonlight. Inscribed inside is a vow that outlasts death itself. Rose petals spiral around it in an unseen wind.

es.text: ¡Oh, espléndido mundo nuevo, que tiene tales gentes!
es.english: O brave new world, that has such people in it!
es.back: O splendid new world, which has such people!
es.controlEnglish: Uneasy lies the head that wears a crown.

es.text: Un anillo de oro descansa en el antepecho de piedra de un balcón y recoge la luz de la luna. Dentro lleva grabado un voto que sobrevive a la muerte misma. Pétalos de rosa giran a su alrededor en un viento invisible.
es.english: A golden ring rests on a stone balcony ledge, catching moonlight. Inscribed inside is a vow that outlasts death itself. Rose petals spiral around it in an unseen wind.
es.back: A golden ring rests on the stone sill of a balcony and collects the moonlight. Inside it carries an engraved vow that survives death itself, rose petals spin around it in an invisible wind.
es.controlEnglish: Three caskets gleam in a candlelit chamber -- gold, silver, and lead. The lead casket hums with quiet truth, rewarding those wise enough to see past appearances.

es.text: El anillo de Romeo
es.english: Romeo's Ring
es.back: Romeo's Ring
es.controlEnglish: Portia's Casket

es.text: Tres cofres relucen en una cámara a la luz de las velas: oro, plata y plomo. El de plomo vibra con una verdad callada y premia a quien sabe ver más allá de las apariencias.
es.english: Three caskets gleam in a candlelit chamber -- gold, silver, and lead. The lead casket hums with quiet truth, rewarding those wise enough to see past appearances.
es.back: Three chests shine in a candlelit chamber: gold, silver and lead; the lead one vibrates with a silent truth and rewards those who know how to see beyond appearances.
es.controlEnglish: A tarnished Scottish crown sits on a bloodstained pillow. It pulses with dark ambition, whispering promises of glory to any hand that dares reach for it.

es.text: El cofre de Portia
es.english: Portia's Casket
es.back: The Chest of Portia
es.controlEnglish: Macbeth's Crown

es.text: Una corona escocesa deslustrada reposa sobre un cojín manchado de sangre. Late con oscura ambición y susurra promesas de gloria a toda mano que se atreva a tomarla.
es.english: A tarnished Scottish crown sits on a bloodstained pillow. It pulses with dark ambition, whispering promises of glory to any hand that dares reach for it.
es.back: A faded Scottish crown rests on a blood-stained cushion, beating with dark ambition and whispering promises of glory to every hand that dares grab it.
es.controlEnglish: An ancient tome bound in sea-weathered leather floats above a stone altar. Its pages turn by themselves, each one summoning a different storm.

es.text: Inquieta yace la cabeza que lleva una corona.
es.english: Uneasy lies the head that wears a crown.
es.back: Restlessly lies the head wearing a crown.
es.controlEnglish: I'll drown my book.

es.text: La corona de Macbeth
es.english: Macbeth's Crown
es.back: The Crown of Macbeth
es.controlEnglish: The Tempest Codex

es.text: Un tomo antiguo, encuadernado en cuero curtido por el mar, flota sobre un altar de piedra. Sus páginas pasan solas, y cada una convoca una tormenta distinta.
es.english: An ancient tome bound in sea-weathered leather floats above a stone altar. Its pages turn by themselves, each one summoning a different storm.
es.back: An ancient volume, bound in sea-tanned leather, floats on a stone altar; its pages pass by themselves, each calling forth a different storm.
es.controlEnglish: A crystal vial holds tears that shimmer like captured starlight. Each drop carries the sorrow of a daughter who loved too truly and spoke too plainly.

es.text: Ahogaré mi libro.
es.english: I'll drown my book.
es.back: I'll drown my book.
es.controlEnglish: O dear father, it is thy business that I go about.

es.text: El códice de la tempestad
es.english: The Tempest Codex
es.back: The Codex of the Storm
es.controlEnglish: Cordelia's Tears

es.text: Un frasco de cristal guarda lágrimas que relucen como luz de estrellas cautiva. Cada gota lleva la pena de una hija que amó con demasiada verdad y habló con demasiada llaneza.
es.english: A crystal vial holds tears that shimmer like captured starlight. Each drop carries the sorrow of a daughter who loved too truly and spoke too plainly.
es.back: A glass jar holds tears that shine like captivating starlight; each drop carries the sorrow of a daughter who loved with too much truth and spoke too plainly.
es.controlEnglish: A donkey-headed mask hangs from a mossy branch in the fairy wood. Whoever dons it sees the world through enchanted eyes -- and becomes irresistible to fairy queens.

es.text: Oh, padre querido, son tus asuntos los que me ocupan.
es.english: O dear father, it is thy business that I go about.
es.back: Oh, dear father, it is your affairs that occupy me.
es.controlEnglish: Bless thee, Bottom! Thou art translated!

es.text: Las lágrimas de Cordelia
es.english: Cordelia's Tears
es.back: The Tears of Cordelia
es.controlEnglish: Bottom's Mask

es.text: Una máscara con cabeza de burro cuelga de una rama musgosa en el bosque de las hadas. Quien se la pone ve el mundo con ojos encantados, y se vuelve irresistible para las reinas de las hadas.
es.english: A donkey-headed mask hangs from a mossy branch in the fairy wood. Whoever dons it sees the world through enchanted eyes -- and becomes irresistible to fairy queens.
es.back: A donkey-headed mask hangs from a mossy branch in the fairy forest; whoever wears it sees the world with enchanted eyes and becomes irresistible to fairy queens.
es.controlEnglish: A gnarled root shaped like a screaming figure is unearthed by candlelight. Soil crumbles away to reveal its twisted, ancient power. The apothecary handles it with trembling reverence.

es.text: ¡Dios te bendiga, Bottom! ¡Estás transformado!
es.english: Bless thee, Bottom! Thou art translated!
es.back: God bless you, Bottom! You're transformed!
es.controlEnglish: Fetch me that flower; the herb I showed thee once.

es.text: La máscara de Bottom
es.english: Bottom's Mask
es.back: The Mask of Bottom
es.controlEnglish: Mandrake Root

es.text: Una raíz nudosa con forma de figura que grita es desenterrada a la luz de una vela. La tierra se desmorona y deja ver su poder antiguo y retorcido. El boticario la maneja con reverencia temblorosa.
es.english: A gnarled root shaped like a screaming figure is unearthed by candlelight. Soil crumbles away to reveal its twisted, ancient power. The apothecary handles it with trembling reverence.
es.back: A knotty root shaped like a screaming figure is dug up in the light of a candle. The earth crumbles and reveals its ancient, twisted power; the pharmacist handles it with trembling reverence.
es.controlEnglish: A dewdrop clings to a moonlit orchid, glowing with otherworldly violet light. One drop upon sleeping eyelids and the dreamer falls in love with the first creature they see.

es.text: Raíz de mandrágora
es.english: Mandrake Root
es.back: Mandragora root
es.controlEnglish: Oberon's Dew

es.text: Una gota de rocío se aferra a una orquídea bañada de luna y brilla con una luz violeta de otro mundo. Una gota sobre los párpados dormidos, y quien sueña se enamora de la primera criatura que ve.
es.english: A dewdrop clings to a moonlit orchid, glowing with otherworldly violet light. One drop upon sleeping eyelids and the dreamer falls in love with the first creature they see.
es.back: A drop of dew clings to a moonlit orchid and shines with an otherworldly violet light; one drop on the sleeping eyelids, and the dreamer falls in love with the first creature he sees.
es.controlEnglish: A black glass vial weeps green vapor in a darkened corridor. The tincture within has toppled kings and shattered dynasties, one silent drop at a time.

es.text: Tráeme aquella flor; la hierba que una vez te mostré.
es.english: Fetch me that flower; the herb I showed thee once.
es.back: Bring me that flower; the grass I once showed you.
es.controlEnglish: Full fathom five thy father lies; of his bones are coral made.

es.text: Rocío de Oberón
es.english: Oberon's Dew
es.back: Rosie of Oberon
es.controlEnglish: Hemlock Tincture

es.text: Un frasco de vidrio negro exhala vapor verde en un corredor a oscuras. La tintura que encierra ha derribado reyes y deshecho dinastías, gota silenciosa a gota silenciosa.
es.english: A black glass vial weeps green vapor in a darkened corridor. The tincture within has toppled kings and shattered dynasties, one silent drop at a time.
es.back: A black glass jar exhales green vapor in a darkened corridor; the tincture it contains has overthrown kings and destroyed dynasties, silent drop by silent drop.
es.controlEnglish: Pale berries glisten among dark evergreen leaves, harvested under a winter moon. The extract hums with the quiet, persistent magic of the natural world.

es.text: Tintura de cicuta
es.english: Hemlock Tincture
es.back: Tincture of cicuta
es.controlEnglish: Mistletoe Extract

es.text: Unas bayas pálidas relucen entre oscuras hojas perennes, recogidas bajo una luna de invierno. El extracto vibra con la magia callada y tenaz del mundo natural.
es.english: Pale berries glisten among dark evergreen leaves, harvested under a winter moon. The extract hums with the quiet, persistent magic of the natural world.
es.back: Pale berries gleam among dark evergreen leaves, gathered under a winter moon.The extract vibrates with the quiet and tenacious magic of the natural world.
es.controlEnglish: A pearl-stoppered flask holds luminous blue liquid that shifts like a living sea. Within it, tiny coral formations grow and dissolve. It smells of salt and forgotten voyages.

es.text: Extracto de muérdago
es.english: Mistletoe Extract
es.back: Mistletoe Extract
es.controlEnglish: Mermaid's Tears

es.text: Un frasco con tapón de perla guarda un líquido azul luminoso que se mueve como un mar vivo. Dentro crecen y se deshacen diminutas formaciones de coral. Huele a sal y a viajes olvidados.
es.english: A pearl-stoppered flask holds luminous blue liquid that shifts like a living sea. Within it, tiny coral formations grow and dissolve. It smells of salt and forgotten voyages.
es.back: A bottle with a pearl stopper holds a luminous blue liquid that moves like a living sea. Inside, tiny coral formations grow and fall apart.It smells of salt and forgotten journeys.
es.controlEnglish: A dusty apothecary shop in Mantua's poorest quarter. A desperate elixir glows amber in a cracked vial, potent enough to bridge the gap between life and death.

es.text: A cinco brazas yace tu padre; de sus huesos se ha hecho coral.
es.english: Full fathom five thy father lies; of his bones are coral made.
es.back: At five arms your father lies; his bones have become coral.
es.controlEnglish: I wandered lonely as a cloud that floats on high o'er vales and hills.

es.text: Lágrimas de sirena
es.english: Mermaid's Tears
es.back: Mermaid Tears
es.controlEnglish: Apothecary's Elixir

es.text: Una polvorienta botica en el barrio más pobre de Mantua. Un elixir desesperado brilla, ambarino, en un frasco agrietado, con fuerza bastante para salvar la distancia entre la vida y la muerte.
es.english: A dusty apothecary shop in Mantua's poorest quarter. A desperate elixir glows amber in a cracked vial, potent enough to bridge the gap between life and death.
es.back: A dusty drugstore in the poorest neighborhood of Mantua: a desperate elixir shines, amber, in a cracked vial, strong enough to bridge the distance between life and death.
es.controlEnglish: A carpet of golden daffodils stretches along the shores of a still lake. Wordsworth walks among them, notebook in hand, the Cumberland fells rising behind him.

es.text: Elixir del boticario
es.english: Apothecary's Elixir
es.back: Elixir of the Pharmacist
es.controlEnglish: Yorick's Skull

es.text: Una alfombra de narcisos dorados se extiende por la orilla de un lago en calma. Wordsworth camina entre ellos, cuaderno en mano, con las colinas de Cumberland alzándose a su espalda.
es.english: A carpet of golden daffodils stretches along the shores of a still lake. Wordsworth walks among them, notebook in hand, the Cumberland fells rising behind him.
es.back: A carpet of golden daffodils stretches along the shore of a calm lake, Wordsworth walking among them, notebook in hand, with the hills of Cumberland rising behind his back.
es.controlEnglish: A becalmed ship drifts on a painted ocean. The Ancient Mariner stares at the albatross around his neck as spectral figures rise from the glassy sea.

es.text: Vagaba solitario como una nube que flota en lo alto sobre valles y colinas.
es.english: I wandered lonely as a cloud that floats on high o'er vales and hills.
es.back: He wandered alone like a cloud that floats high over valleys and hills.
es.controlEnglish: Water, water, every where, nor any drop to drink.

es.text: Un barco en calma chicha deriva sobre un océano pintado. El viejo marinero mira el albatros que lleva al cuello mientras figuras espectrales suben del mar de vidrio.
es.english: A becalmed ship drifts on a painted ocean. The Ancient Mariner stares at the albatross around his neck as spectral figures rise from the glassy sea.
es.back: The old sailor watches the albatross he wears around his neck as spectral figures rise from the sea of glass.
es.controlEnglish: A Hampstead garden in autumn. Keats sits beneath a plum tree, writing feverishly as a nightingale sings from the darkening branches above.

es.text: Agua, agua por todas partes, y ni una gota que beber.
es.english: Water, water, every where, nor any drop to drink.
es.back: Water, water everywhere, and not a drop to drink.
es.controlEnglish: A thing of beauty is a joy for ever: its loveliness increases.

es.text: Un jardín de Hampstead en otoño. Keats, sentado bajo un ciruelo, escribe con fiebre mientras un ruiseñor canta desde las ramas que oscurecen.
es.english: A Hampstead garden in autumn. Keats sits beneath a plum tree, writing feverishly as a nightingale sings from the darkening branches above.
es.back: A Hampstead garden in autumn, Keats sitting under a plum tree writing feverishly as a nightingale sings from the darkening branches.
es.controlEnglish: A Venetian palazzo at midnight. Byron stands on the balcony, cape billowing, gazing across the dark canal. A half-finished manuscript burns in the fireplace behind him.

es.text: Una cosa bella es un gozo para siempre: su encanto crece.
es.english: A thing of beauty is a joy for ever: its loveliness increases.
es.back: A beautiful thing is a joy forever: its charm grows.
es.controlEnglish: She walks in beauty, like the night of cloudless climes and starry skies.

es.text: Un palacio veneciano a medianoche. Byron está en el balcón, con la capa al viento, mirando el canal oscuro. A su espalda, un manuscrito a medio terminar arde en la chimenea.
es.english: A Venetian palazzo at midnight. Byron stands on the balcony, cape billowing, gazing across the dark canal. A half-finished manuscript burns in the fireplace behind him.
es.back: A Venetian palace at midnight. Byron is on the balcony, with his cloak in the wind, looking out over the dark canal; behind him, a half-finished manuscript burns in the chimney.
es.controlEnglish: A candlelit study in Geneva during a thunderstorm. Mary writes by lightning flash as the creature stirs in the shadows behind her. Science and horror become one.

es.text: Camina en la belleza, como la noche de climas sin nubes y cielos estrellados.
es.english: She walks in beauty, like the night of cloudless climes and starry skies.
es.back: Walk in beauty, like the night of cloudless weather and starry skies.
es.controlEnglish: Beware; for I am fearless, and therefore powerful.

es.text: Un estudio a la luz de las velas en Ginebra, durante una tormenta. Mary escribe al fulgor de los relámpagos mientras la criatura se agita en las sombras detrás de ella. Ciencia y horror se hacen uno.
es.english: A candlelit study in Geneva during a thunderstorm. Mary writes by lightning flash as the creature stirs in the shadows behind her. Science and horror become one.
es.back: A candlelit study in Geneva, during a storm. Mary writes in the glare of lightning while the creature waves in the shadows behind her.Science and horror become one.
es.controlEnglish: A dim chamber lit by a dying fire. Poe sits hunched at his desk as a raven alights on the bust of Pallas. The word "Nevermore" echoes in the shadows.

es.text: Cuidado; pues no tengo miedo, y por eso soy poderoso.
es.english: Beware; for I am fearless, and therefore powerful.
es.back: Beware; for I am not afraid, and therefore I am mighty.
es.controlEnglish: To see a World in a Grain of Sand and a Heaven in a Wild Flower.

es.text: Una estancia en penumbra, alumbrada por un fuego que muere. Poe está encorvado sobre su escritorio cuando un cuervo se posa en el busto de Palas. La palabra «Nunca más» resuena en las sombras.
es.english: A dim chamber lit by a dying fire. Poe sits hunched at his desk as a raven alights on the bust of Pallas. The word "Nevermore" echoes in the shadows.
es.back: A half-dark room, lit by a dying fire. Poe is bent over his desk when a crow lands on the bust of Palas and the word “Never Again” echoes in the shadows.
es.controlEnglish: A London printing workshop ablaze with visionary light. Blake etches a tiger into copper as the beast materializes from the plate, burning bright in the forests of the night.

es.text: Un taller de imprenta de Londres encendido de luz visionaria. Blake graba un tigre en el cobre mientras la fiera sale de la plancha, ardiendo brillante en los bosques de la noche.
es.english: A London printing workshop ablaze with visionary light. Blake etches a tiger into copper as the beast materializes from the plate, burning bright in the forests of the night.
es.back: A London printing shop lit with visionary light, Blake engraving a tiger on copper as the beast comes out of the press, burning bright in the woods at night.
es.controlEnglish: A windswept Italian clifftop. Shelley faces the storm, arms wide, as the west wind tears pages from his notebook and scatters them across the Mediterranean.

es.text: Ver un mundo en un grano de arena y un cielo en una flor silvestre.
es.english: To see a World in a Grain of Sand and a Heaven in a Wild Flower.
es.back: See a world in a grain of sand and a sky in a wild flower.
es.controlEnglish: If Winter comes, can Spring be far behind?

es.text: Un acantilado italiano azotado por el viento. Shelley encara la tormenta con los brazos abiertos mientras el viento del oeste arranca las hojas de su cuaderno y las esparce por el Mediterráneo.
es.english: A windswept Italian clifftop. Shelley faces the storm, arms wide, as the west wind tears pages from his notebook and scatters them across the Mediterranean.
es.back: A windswept Italian cliff, Shelley faces the storm with open arms as the west wind tears the leaves from her notebook and scatters them across the Mediterranean.
es.controlEnglish: A sunlit room in Florence. Elizabeth writes at a window overlooking the Arno, her spaniel at her feet. Love letters from Robert lie open on the desk.

es.text: Si llega el invierno, ¿puede estar lejos la primavera?
es.english: If Winter comes, can Spring be far behind?
es.back: If winter comes, can spring be far away?
es.controlEnglish: How do I love thee? Let me count the ways.

es.text: Una habitación soleada en Florencia. Elizabeth escribe junto a una ventana que da al Arno, con su spaniel a los pies. Las cartas de amor de Robert están abiertas sobre el escritorio.
es.english: A sunlit room in Florence. Elizabeth writes at a window overlooking the Arno, her spaniel at her feet. Love letters from Robert lie open on the desk.
es.back: A sunny room in Florence. Elizabeth is writing by a window overlooking the Arno, with her spaniel at her feet; Robert’s love letters are open on the desk.
es.controlEnglish: A Pre-Raphaelite garden in fading autumn light. Christina sits among fallen leaves, composing verses that ache with beauty and quiet resignation.

es.text: ¿Cómo te amo? Déjame contar las maneras.
es.english: How do I love thee? Let me count the ways.
es.back: How do I love you? Let me tell the ways.
es.controlEnglish: Remember me when I am gone away, gone far away into the silent land.

es.text: Un jardín prerrafaelita en la luz que se apaga del otoño. Christina está sentada entre hojas caídas, componiendo versos que duelen de belleza y de serena resignación.
es.english: A Pre-Raphaelite garden in fading autumn light. Christina sits among fallen leaves, composing verses that ache with beauty and quiet resignation.
es.back: A Pre-Raphaelite garden in the fading light of autumn, Christina sits among fallen leaves, composing verses that hurt with beauty and serene resignation.
es.controlEnglish: Mount Olympus splits the sky. Zeus sits on a throne of clouds, lightning arcing between his fingers. Below, the mortal world trembles at his gaze.

es.text: Recuérdame cuando me haya ido, ido lejos, a la tierra silenciosa.
es.english: Remember me when I am gone away, gone far away into the silent land.
es.back: Remember me when I'm gone, gone far, to the silent land.
es.controlEnglish: I am the cloud-gatherer, lord of the wide heavens.

es.text: El monte Olimpo parte el cielo. Zeus está sentado en un trono de nubes, con el rayo saltando entre sus dedos. Abajo, el mundo mortal tiembla bajo su mirada.
es.english: Mount Olympus splits the sky. Zeus sits on a throne of clouds, lightning arcing between his fingers. Below, the mortal world trembles at his gaze.
es.back: Mount Olympus splits the sky. Zeus sits on a throne of clouds, with lightning leaping between his fingers; below, the mortal world trembleth under his gaze.
es.controlEnglish: The Parthenon gleams in golden light. Athena stands in full armor, her owl perched on her shield, her grey eyes seeing through every mortal deception.

es.text: Soy el que amontona las nubes, señor de los anchos cielos.
es.english: I am the cloud-gatherer, lord of the wide heavens.
es.back: I am the one who heaps up the clouds, Lord of the wide heavens.
es.controlEnglish: The owl of wisdom takes flight only at dusk.

es.text: El Partenón reluce en una luz dorada. Atenea está de pie con la armadura completa, la lechuza posada en su escudo y los ojos grises viendo a través de todo engaño mortal.
es.english: The Parthenon gleams in golden light. Athena stands in full armor, her owl perched on her shield, her grey eyes seeing through every mortal deception.
es.back: The Parthenon shines in a golden light, Athena stands in full armor, the owl on her shield and gray eyes seeing through all mortal deception.
es.controlEnglish: A golden chariot races across the dawn sky. Apollo plays his lyre as sunlight pours from the wheels, painting the world in color.

es.text: La lechuza de la sabiduría solo alza el vuelo al anochecer.
es.english: The owl of wisdom takes flight only at dusk.
es.back: The owl of wisdom takes flight only at dusk.
es.controlEnglish: I am the god of song, of healing, and of the radiant sun.

es.text: Un carro de oro cruza veloz el cielo del alba. Apolo tañe la lira mientras la luz del sol mana de las ruedas y pinta el mundo de color.
es.english: A golden chariot races across the dawn sky. Apollo plays his lyre as sunlight pours from the wheels, painting the world in color.
es.back: A golden chariot speeds across the dawn sky, Apollo tuning his lyre as sunlight gushes from the wheels and paints the world in colour.
es.controlEnglish: The shores of Cyprus at dawn. Aphrodite rises from sea foam, doves circling above as waves lay pearls at her feet. The world holds its breath.

es.text: Soy el dios del canto, de la curación y del sol radiante.
es.english: I am the god of song, of healing, and of the radiant sun.
es.back: I am the god of singing, healing and the radiant sun.
es.controlEnglish: Even the gods cannot resist the power of love.

es.text: Las costas de Chipre al amanecer. Afrodita surge de la espuma del mar; las palomas vuelan en círculo y las olas dejan perlas a sus pies. El mundo contiene el aliento.
es.english: The shores of Cyprus at dawn. Aphrodite rises from sea foam, doves circling above as waves lay pearls at her feet. The world holds its breath.
es.back: The shores of Cyprus at dawn. Aphrodite rises from the foam of the sea; doves fly in circles and waves leave pearls at her feet.The world holds her breath.
es.controlEnglish: A blur of winged sandals across the sky. Hermes weaves between thunderbolts, a divine message clutched in one hand and a thief's grin on his face.

es.text: Ni siquiera los dioses pueden resistir el poder del amor.
es.english: Even the gods cannot resist the power of love.
es.back: Not even the gods can resist the power of love.
es.controlEnglish: Swift as thought, I carry the words of gods to mortal ears.

es.text: Un borrón de sandalias aladas cruza el cielo. Hermes zigzaguea entre los rayos, con un mensaje divino apretado en una mano y una sonrisa de ladrón en la cara.
es.english: A blur of winged sandals across the sky. Hermes weaves between thunderbolts, a divine message clutched in one hand and a thief's grin on his face.
es.back: A blob of winged sandals crosses the sky, Hermes zigzagging among the rays, a divine message clenched in one hand and a thief's smile on his face.
es.controlEnglish: The throne room of the Underworld, lit by rivers of pale fire. Hades sits with Cerberus at his feet, his helm of darkness on the armrest. The dead file past in endless silence.

es.text: Veloz como el pensamiento, llevo las palabras de los dioses a oídos mortales.
es.english: Swift as thought, I carry the words of gods to mortal ears.
es.back: Fast as thought, I carry the words of the gods to mortal ears.
es.controlEnglish: All souls come to me in the end. I am patient.

es.text: El salón del trono del Inframundo, alumbrado por ríos de fuego pálido. Hades está sentado con Cerbero a sus pies y el yelmo de oscuridad sobre el brazo del trono. Los muertos desfilan en un silencio sin fin.
es.english: The throne room of the Underworld, lit by rivers of pale fire. Hades sits with Cerberus at his feet, his helm of darkness on the armrest. The dead file past in endless silence.
es.back: The throne hall of the Underworld, lit by rivers of pale fire. Hades sits with Cerberus at his feet and the helmet of darkness on the arm of the throne.
es.controlEnglish: A throne split between spring and shadow. Persephone holds a pomegranate in one hand and a crown of flowers in the other, queen of two realms.

es.text: Todas las almas vienen a mí al final. Soy paciente.
es.english: All souls come to me in the end. I am patient.
es.back: All souls come to me in the end. I am patient.
es.controlEnglish: Six seeds I ate, and bound myself between two worlds forever.

es.text: Un trono partido entre la primavera y la sombra. Perséfone sostiene una granada en una mano y una corona de flores en la otra, reina de dos reinos.
es.english: A throne split between spring and shadow. Persephone holds a pomegranate in one hand and a crown of flowers in the other, queen of two realms.
es.back: A throne divided between spring and shade, Persephone holding a pomegranate in one hand and a crown of flowers in the other, queen of two kingdoms.
es.controlEnglish: A storm-battered ship rounds a rocky headland. Odysseus lashes himself to the mast as the Sirens sing from the cliffs. His eyes burn with the memory of Ithaca.

es.text: Seis semillas comí, y me até para siempre entre dos mundos.
es.english: Six seeds I ate, and bound myself between two worlds forever.
es.back: Six seeds I ate, and tied myself forever between two worlds.
es.controlEnglish: Tell me, O Muse, of the man of many ways, who wandered far.

es.text: Un barco maltratado por la tormenta dobla un cabo rocoso. Odiseo se ata al mástil mientras las sirenas cantan desde los acantilados. En sus ojos arde el recuerdo de Ítaca.
es.english: A storm-battered ship rounds a rocky headland. Odysseus lashes himself to the mast as the Sirens sing from the cliffs. His eyes burn with the memory of Ithaca.
es.back: Odysseus is tied to the mast as the sirens sing from the cliffs. The memory of Ithaca burns in his eyes, but he can’t stop crying.
es.controlEnglish: A ruined temple at the edge of the world. Medusa turns, her serpent hair hissing. Stone warriors litter the floor, frozen in their final charge.

es.text: Háblame, oh Musa, del hombre de muchos caminos, que anduvo errante muy lejos.
es.english: Tell me, O Muse, of the man of many ways, who wandered far.
es.back: Tell me, O Moses, of the man of many ways, who wandered far and wide.
es.controlEnglish: Look upon me, if you dare. My gaze is the last thing you will see.

es.text: Un templo en ruinas al borde del mundo. Medusa se vuelve, con su cabellera de serpientes silbando. Guerreros de piedra cubren el suelo, congelados en su última carga.
es.english: A ruined temple at the edge of the world. Medusa turns, her serpent hair hissing. Stone warriors litter the floor, frozen in their final charge.
es.back: A ruined temple at the edge of the world. Medusa turns, her snake hair whistling, stone warriors cover the ground, frozen in their last charge.
es.controlEnglish: The plains of Troy at dawn. Achilles charges in blazing armor, his war cry splitting the air. Behind him, Greek ships burn on the shore.

es.text: Mírame, si te atreves. Mi mirada es lo último que verás.
es.english: Look upon me, if you dare. My gaze is the last thing you will see.
es.back: Look at me, if you dare. My look is the last thing you'll see.
es.controlEnglish: I would rather live a short life of glory than a long life forgotten.

es.text: Las llanuras de Troya al amanecer. Aquiles carga con armadura resplandeciente y su grito de guerra parte el aire. Detrás de él, las naves griegas arden en la orilla.
es.english: The plains of Troy at dawn. Achilles charges in blazing armor, his war cry splitting the air. Behind him, Greek ships burn on the shore.
es.back: The plains of Troy at dawn. Achilles loaded in shining armor and his cry of war breaks the air, behind him, the Greek ships are burning on the shore.
es.controlEnglish: A grand stage materializes. The Sonnet Man steps forward from a golden spotlight, microphone in hand. Shakespeare's words transform into hip-hop bars as the crowd cheers.

es.text: Prefiero vivir una vida corta de gloria que una vida larga en el olvido.
es.english: I would rather live a short life of glory than a long life forgotten.
es.back: I would rather live a short life of glory than a long life in oblivion.
es.controlEnglish: Shall I compare thee to a summer's day?
