pt.text: Um grande palco se materializa. The Sonnet Man avança de um foco dourado, com o microfone na mão. As palavras de Shakespeare se transformam em rimas de hip-hop enquanto a multidão aplaude.
pt.english: A grand stage materializes. The Sonnet Man steps forward from a golden spotlight, microphone in hand. Shakespeare's words transform into hip-hop bars as the crowd cheers.
pt.back: A grand stage materializes. The Sonnet Man advances from a golden spotlight, with the microphone in his hand.The words of Shakespeare turn into hip-hop rhymes as the crowd applauds.
pt.controlEnglish: A moonlit balcony scene unfolds. Romeo reaches upward as Juliet appears above. Rose petals drift through the air. The scene pulses with a warm crimson glow.

pt.text: Devo comparar-te a um dia de verão?
pt.english: Shall I compare thee to a summer's day?
pt.back: Should I compare you to a summer day?
pt.controlEnglish: But soft, what light through yonder window breaks?

pt.text: Uma cena de sacada ao luar se desenrola. Romeu estende a mão para o alto enquanto Julieta aparece acima dele. Pétalas de rosa flutuam no ar. A cena pulsa com um brilho carmesim e quente.
pt.english: A moonlit balcony scene unfolds. Romeo reaches upward as Juliet appears above. Rose petals drift through the air. The scene pulses with a warm crimson glow.
pt.back: A moonlit balcony scene unfolds. Romeo reaches up as Juliet appears above him, rose petals float in the air, and the scene pulses with a warm crimson glow.
pt.controlEnglish: The Capulet garden blooms in moonlight. Juliet stands among roses, her eyes bright with defiance. A nightingale sings from the branches above.

pt.text: Mas, silêncio! Que luz irrompe por aquela janela?
pt.english: But soft, what light through yonder window breaks?
pt.back: But, silence! What light breaks through that window?
pt.controlEnglish: What's in a name? That which we call a rose...

pt.text: O jardim dos Capuleto floresce ao luar. Julieta está entre as rosas, com os olhos brilhando de desafio. Um rouxinol canta nos galhos.
pt.english: The Capulet garden blooms in moonlight. Juliet stands among roses, her eyes bright with defiance. A nightingale sings from the branches above.
pt.back: The garden of the Capulets blooms in the moonlight. Juliet stands among the roses, her eyes shining with defiance; a nightingale sings on the branches.
pt.controlEnglish: The castle of Elsinore emerges from shadow. Hamlet stands at the battlements, Yorick's skull hovering beside him. A spectral figure appears on the ramparts above.

pt.text: O que há num nome? Aquilo que chamamos de rosa...
pt.english: What's in a name? That which we call a rose...
pt.back: What's in a name? What we call a rose...
pt.controlEnglish: A plague on both your houses!

pt.text: O castelo de Elsinore surge da sombra. Hamlet está nas ameias, com a caveira de Yorick pairando ao seu lado. Uma figura espectral aparece nas muralhas.
pt.english: The castle of Elsinore emerges from shadow. Hamlet stands at the battlements, Yorick's skull hovering beside him. A spectral figure appears on the ramparts above.
pt.back: The castle of Elsinore emerges from the shadows. Hamlet is in the walls, with Yorick's skull hovering beside him, and a spectral figure appears on the walls.
pt.controlEnglish: A gentle stream winds through a willow grove. Ophelia floats among wildflowers, whispering forgotten verses. Petals circle in the current.

pt.text: Um riacho manso serpenteia por um bosque de salgueiros. Ofélia flutua entre flores silvestres, sussurrando versos esquecidos. As pétalas rodopiam na correnteza.
pt.english: A gentle stream winds through a willow grove. Ophelia floats among wildflowers, whispering forgotten verses. Petals circle in the current.
pt.back: A gentle stream meanders through a willow grove. Ophelia floats among wild flowers, whispering forgotten verses.The petals swirl in the current.
pt.controlEnglish: A Verona street erupts in chaos. Mercutio dances between blades, laughing in the face of danger. Sparks fly from clashing steel.

pt.text: Uma rua de Verona irrompe em caos. Mercutio dança entre as lâminas, rindo na cara do perigo. Saltam faíscas do aço que se choca.
pt.english: A Verona street erupts in chaos. Mercutio dances between blades, laughing in the face of danger. Sparks fly from clashing steel.
pt.back: A street in Verona bursts into chaos. Mercutio dances between the blades, laughing in the face of the danger.
pt.controlEnglish: The enchanted forest shimmers with mischief. Puck darts between ancient oaks, leaving trails of pixie dust. Sleeping mortals dream strange dreams below.

pt.text: Uma praga sobre vossas duas casas!
pt.english: A plague on both your houses!
pt.back: A plague upon your two houses!
pt.controlEnglish: Lord, what fools these mortals be!

pt.text: A floresta encantada cintila de travessura. Puck se esgueira entre carvalhos antigos, deixando rastros de pó de fada. Lá embaixo, mortais adormecidos sonham sonhos estranhos.
pt.english: The enchanted forest shimmers with mischief. Puck darts between ancient oaks, leaving trails of pixie dust. Sleeping mortals dream strange dreams below.
pt.back: The enchanted forest sparkles with mischief. Puck sneaks through ancient oaks, leaving traces of fairy dust.Below, sleeping mortals dream strange dreams.
pt.controlEnglish: A throne of living vines rises from the forest floor. Titania commands her fairy court as fireflies illuminate the canopy. Nature itself bows to her will.

pt.text: Senhor, que tolos são estes mortais!
pt.english: Lord, what fools these mortals be!
pt.back: Lord, how foolish these mortals are!
pt.controlEnglish: Come, sit thee down upon this flowery bed.

pt.text: Um trono de trepadeiras vivas se ergue do chão da floresta. Titania comanda sua corte de fadas enquanto os vaga-lumes iluminam a copa das árvores. A própria natureza se curva à sua vontade.
pt.english: A throne of living vines rises from the forest floor. Titania commands her fairy court as fireflies illuminate the canopy. Nature itself bows to her will.
pt.back: A throne of living climbers rises from the forest floor. Titania commands her fairy court as fireflies illuminate the treetops, and nature itself bows to her will.
pt.controlEnglish: A skull rests on velvet in a dim crypt. Ghostly laughter echoes as memories of the court jester flicker like candlelight.

pt.text: Vem, senta-te neste leito florido.
pt.english: Come, sit thee down upon this flowery bed.
pt.back: Come, sit on this flower bed.
pt.controlEnglish: Now my charms are all o'erthrown.

pt.text: Uma caveira repousa sobre veludo numa cripta sombria. Um riso fantasmagórico ecoa enquanto as memórias do bobo da corte tremeluzem como a luz de uma vela.
pt.english: A skull rests on velvet in a dim crypt. Ghostly laughter echoes as memories of the court jester flicker like candlelight.
pt.back: A skull rests on velvet in a gloomy crypt, ghostly laughter echoes as the memories of the court fool glisten like candlelight.
pt.controlEnglish: A gnarled staff crackles with arcane energy. The tempest swirls around it as Prospero whispers his final spell. Lightning splits the sky.

pt.text: A caveira de Yorick
pt.english: Yorick's Skull
pt.back: The Skull of Yorick
pt.controlEnglish: Prospero's Staff

pt.text: Um cajado nodoso crepita de energia arcana. A tempestade rodopia à sua volta enquanto Próspero sussurra seu último feitiço. O relâmpago rasga o céu.
pt.english: A gnarled staff crackles with arcane energy. The tempest swirls around it as Prospero whispers his final spell. Lightning splits the sky.
pt.back: A knotty wand crackles of arcane energy. The storm swirls around him as Prospero whispers his last spell, and lightning tears the sky apart.
pt.controlEnglish: A glowing vial pulses with rose-colored light. Hearts drift upward from its surface as a sweet melody fills the air.

pt.text: Agora meus encantos estão todos desfeitos.
pt.english: Now my charms are all o'erthrown.
pt.back: Now my charms are all undone.
pt.controlEnglish: The course of true love never did run smooth.

pt.text: O cajado de Próspero
pt.english: Prospero's Staff
pt.back: The staff of Prospero
pt.controlEnglish: Love Potion

pt.text: Um frasco luminoso pulsa com luz rosada. Corações sobem de sua superfície enquanto uma doce melodia enche o ar.
pt.english: A glowing vial pulses with rose-colored light. Hearts drift upward from its surface as a sweet melody fills the air.
pt.back: A luminous flask pulses with pink light, hearts rise from its surface as a sweet melody fills the air.
pt.controlEnglish: A bubbling cauldron belches green smoke. Three shadowy figures circle it, chanting. Eyes glow from the dark woods beyond.

pt.text: O curso do verdadeiro amor nunca correu sereno.
pt.english: The course of true love never did run smooth.
pt.back: The course of true love has never been smooth.
pt.controlEnglish: Double, double toil and trouble.

pt.text: Poção do amor
pt.english: Love Potion
pt.back: Potion of love
pt.controlEnglish: Witches' Brew

pt.text: Um caldeirão borbulhante solta fumaça verde. Três figuras sombrias o rodeiam, entoando cânticos. Olhos brilham na floresta escura.
pt.english: A bubbling cauldron belches green smoke. Three shadowy figures circle it, chanting. Eyes glow from the dark woods beyond.
pt.back: A bubbling cauldron releases green smoke. Three gloomy figures surround him, singing songs.Eyes shine in the dark forest.
pt.controlEnglish: The Prince stands on the steps of Verona's palace, his voice commanding silence over the feuding crowd. A golden scepter burns with authority.

pt.text: Dobra, dobra, canseira e tormento.
pt.english: Double, double toil and trouble.
pt.back: Bend, bend, fatigue and torment.
pt.controlEnglish: If ever you disturb our streets again, your lives shall pay the forfeit of the peace.

pt.text: Caldo das bruxas
pt.english: Witches' Brew
pt.back: Broth of witches
pt.controlEnglish: Dagger of the Mind

pt.text: O Príncipe está nos degraus do palácio de Verona; sua voz impõe silêncio à multidão em conflito. Um cetro dourado arde de autoridade.
pt.english: The Prince stands on the steps of Verona's palace, his voice commanding silence over the feuding crowd. A golden scepter burns with authority.
pt.back: The Prince stands on the steps of the palace of Verona; his voice imposes silence upon the conflicting crowd; a golden scepter burns with authority.
pt.controlEnglish: A candlelit cell in a monastery. The Friar tends his garden of herbs and poisons, wisdom etched into his weathered face.

pt.text: Se alguma vez voltardes a perturbar nossas ruas, vossas vidas pagarão pela quebra da paz.
pt.english: If ever you disturb our streets again, your lives shall pay the forfeit of the peace.
pt.back: If you ever disturb our streets again, your lives will pay for the breach of peace.
pt.controlEnglish: These violent delights have violent ends.

pt.text: Uma cela de mosteiro à luz de velas. O frade cuida de seu jardim de ervas e venenos, com a sabedoria gravada no rosto curtido pelo tempo.
pt.english: A candlelit cell in a monastery. The Friar tends his garden of herbs and poisons, wisdom etched into his weathered face.
pt.back: The monk takes care of his garden of herbs and poisons, with the wisdom engraved on his face tanned by time.
pt.controlEnglish: A warm kitchen in the Capulet house. The Nurse bustles with fierce devotion, a secret letter tucked in her apron.

pt.text: Estes prazeres violentos têm fins violentos.
pt.english: These violent delights have violent ends.
pt.back: These violent pleasures have violent ends.
pt.controlEnglish: I am the drudge and toil in your delight.

pt.text: Uma cozinha acolhedora na casa dos Capuleto. A ama anda atarefada com devoção feroz, uma carta secreta guardada no avental.
pt.english: A warm kitchen in the Capulet house. The Nurse bustles with fierce devotion, a secret letter tucked in her apron.
pt.back: A cozy kitchen in the house of Capulet.The mistress is busy with ferocious devotion, a secret letter kept in the apron.
pt.controlEnglish: An island shrouded in tempest. Prospero raises his hands as lightning obeys his will, the sea churning at his command.

pt.text: Sou eu a escrava que se cansa por vosso deleite.
pt.english: I am the drudge and toil in your delight.
pt.back: I am the slave who is weary for your delight.
pt.controlEnglish: We are such stuff as dreams are made on.

pt.text: Uma ilha envolta em tempestade. Próspero ergue as mãos enquanto o relâmpago obedece à sua vontade e o mar se agita a seu comando.
pt.english: An island shrouded in tempest. Prospero raises his hands as lightning obeys his will, the sea churning at his command.
pt.back: An island enveloped in a storm, Prospero raises his hands as the lightning obeys his will and the sea roars at his command.
pt.controlEnglish: A shimmering spirit dissolves into wind and light, reforming as music. Ariel dances between the visible and invisible.

pt.text: Somos feitos da matéria de que são feitos os sonhos.
pt.english: We are such stuff as dreams are made on.
pt.back: We are made of the matter that dreams are made of.
pt.controlEnglish: All hail, great master! Grave sir, hail!

pt.text: Um espírito cintilante se dissolve em vento e luz e se refaz em música. Ariel dança entre o visível e o invisível.
pt.english: A shimmering spirit dissolves into wind and light, reforming as music. Ariel dances between the visible and invisible.
pt.back: A sparkling spirit dissolves in wind and light and re-makes itself into music.Ariel dances between the visible and the invisible.
pt.controlEnglish: A cave mouth on a wild shore. Caliban crouches among the rocks, eyes burning with resentment and primal intelligence.

pt.text: Salve, grande amo! Grave senhor, salve!
pt.english: All hail, great master! Grave sir, hail!
pt.back: Hail, great master! Grave lord, hail!
pt.controlEnglish: This island's mine, by Sycorax my mother.

pt.text: A boca de uma caverna numa costa selvagem. Caliban se agacha entre as rochas, com os olhos ardendo de rancor e de uma inteligência primitiva.
pt.english: A cave mouth on a wild shore. Caliban crouches among the rocks, eyes burning with resentment and primal intelligence.
pt.back: The mouth of a cave on a wild coast, Caliban crouches among the rocks, his eyes burning with resentment and primitive intelligence.
pt.controlEnglish: A Verona plaza at dawn. Benvolio stands between drawn swords, his open hands the only weapon against the gathering storm.

pt.text: Esta ilha é minha, por Sycorax, minha mãe.
pt.english: This island's mine, by Sycorax my mother.
pt.back: This island is mine, by Sycorax, my mother.
pt.controlEnglish: I do but keep the peace. Put up thy sword.

pt.text: Uma praça de Verona ao amanhecer. Benvolio está entre espadas desembainhadas; suas mãos abertas são a única arma contra a tempestade que se forma.
pt.english: A Verona plaza at dawn. Benvolio stands between drawn swords, his open hands the only weapon against the gathering storm.
pt.back: A square of Verona at dawn.Benvolio stands among unsheathed swords; his open hands are the only weapon against the storm that is forming.
pt.controlEnglish: A Verona alley ablaze with torchlight. Tybalt draws his rapier with lethal grace, his eyes fixed on his enemy.

pt.text: Eu só mantenho a paz. Guarda tua espada.
pt.english: I do but keep the peace. Put up thy sword.
pt.back: I'm just keeping the peace.
pt.controlEnglish: What, drawn, and talk of peace? I hate the word.

pt.text: Uma viela de Verona ardendo à luz das tochas. Tybalt saca o florete com graça letal, de olhos fixos no inimigo.
pt.english: A Verona alley ablaze with torchlight. Tybalt draws his rapier with lethal grace, his eyes fixed on his enemy.
pt.back: An alley of Verona burning in the light of torches, Tybalt pulls out the floret with lethal grace, eyes fixed on the enemy.
pt.controlEnglish: The throne room of Elsinore, draped in false splendor. Claudius grips the crown, a vial of poison hidden in his robes.

pt.text: O quê? De espada na mão, e falas de paz? Odeio essa palavra.
pt.english: What, drawn, and talk of peace? I hate the word.
pt.back: What? With a sword in your hand, and you speak of peace? I hate that word.
pt.controlEnglish: Ill met by moonlight, proud Titania.

pt.text: A sala do trono de Elsinore, coberta de falso esplendor. Claudius agarra a coroa, com um frasco de veneno escondido nas vestes.
pt.english: The throne room of Elsinore, draped in false splendor. Claudius grips the crown, a vial of poison hidden in his robes.
pt.back: The throne room of Elsinore, covered in false splendor.Claudius grabs the crown, with a vial of poison hidden in his garments.
pt.controlEnglish: A moonlit glade deep in the enchanted forest. Oberon materializes from shadow, his crown of antlers catching silver light.

pt.text: Uma clareira ao luar, no fundo da floresta encantada. Oberon surge da sombra; sua coroa de galhadas capta a luz prateada.
pt.english: A moonlit glade deep in the enchanted forest. Oberon materializes from shadow, his crown of antlers catching silver light.
pt.back: A moonlit clearing at the bottom of the enchanted forest. Oberon emerges from the shadow. His crown of twigs catches the silvery light.
pt.controlEnglish: A spectral dagger floats in darkness, its blade dripping with phantom blood. Macbeth's hand reaches but can never grasp it.

pt.text: Mau encontro ao luar, orgulhosa Titania.
pt.english: Ill met by moonlight, proud Titania.
pt.back: Bad encounter at moonlight, proud Titania.
pt.controlEnglish: Is this a dagger which I see before me?

pt.text: Um punhal espectral flutua na escuridão, com a lâmina pingando sangue fantasma. A mão de Macbeth se estende, mas nunca consegue agarrá-lo.
pt.english: A spectral dagger floats in darkness, its blade dripping with phantom blood. Macbeth's hand reaches but can never grasp it.
pt.back: A spectral dagger floats in the darkness, with the blade dripping ghost blood; Macbeth's hand reaches for it, but never gets hold of it.
pt.controlEnglish: A crushed purple flower drips iridescent nectar into a waiting palm. Wherever it falls, eyes change — and hearts follow.

pt.text: É um punhal o que vejo diante de mim?
pt.english: Is this a dagger which I see before me?
pt.back: Is it a dagger I see in front of me?
pt.controlEnglish: I'll put a girdle round about the earth in forty minutes.

pt.text: O punhal da mente
pt.english: Dagger of the Mind
pt.back: The dagger of the mind
pt.controlEnglish: Puck's Flower Juice

pt.text: Uma flor púrpura esmagada pinga néctar iridescente numa palma à espera. Onde quer que caia, os olhos mudam, e os corações os seguem.
pt.english: A crushed purple flower drips iridescent nectar into a waiting palm. Wherever it falls, eyes change — and hearts follow.
pt.back: A crushed purple flower drips iridescent nectar on a waiting palm.Wherever it falls, eyes change, and hearts follow them.
pt.controlEnglish: A bloodstained throne room in Dunsinane. Macbeth grips his sword with trembling hands, the crown heavy on his brow. Birnam Wood stirs on the distant hill.

pt.text: Porei um cinto em volta da terra em quarenta minutos.
pt.english: I'll put a girdle round about the earth in forty minutes.
pt.back: I'll put a belt around the earth in forty minutes.
pt.controlEnglish: I dare do all that may become a man; who dares do more is none.

pt.text: Suco da flor de Puck
pt.english: Puck's Flower Juice
pt.back: Juice of Puck Flower
pt.controlEnglish: Lord Montague

pt.text: Uma sala do trono manchada de sangue em Dunsinane. Macbeth segura a espada com mãos trêmulas, a coroa pesada na fronte. A floresta de Birnam se move na colina distante.
pt.english: A bloodstained throne room in Dunsinane. Macbeth grips his sword with trembling hands, the crown heavy on his brow. Birnam Wood stirs on the distant hill.
pt.back: A blood-stained throne room in Dunsinane. Macbeth holds the sword with trembling hands, the crown heavy on his forehead.The forest of Birnam moves on the distant hill.
pt.controlEnglish: A candlelit chamber in the Scottish castle. Lady Macbeth paces the cold stones, wringing phantom bloodstains from her hands. Shadows cling to her like a second skin.

pt.text: Ouso tudo o que convém a um homem; quem ousa mais não o é.
pt.english: I dare do all that may become a man; who dares do more is none.
pt.back: I dare everything that suits a man; whoever dares more is not a man.
pt.controlEnglish: Come, you spirits that tend on mortal thoughts, unsex me here.

pt.text: Um aposento do castelo escocês à luz de velas. Lady Macbeth anda de um lado para o outro sobre as pedras frias, esfregando das mãos manchas de sangue imaginárias. As sombras se colam a ela como uma segunda pele.
pt.english: A candlelit chamber in the Scottish castle. Lady Macbeth paces the cold stones, wringing phantom bloodstains from her hands. Shadows cling to her like a second skin.
pt.back: A candlelit chamber in the Scottish castle. Lady Macbeth walks back and forth on the cold rocks, rubbing imaginary blood stains from her hands; the shadows cling to her like a second skin.
pt.controlEnglish: A misty Scottish heath at twilight. Banquo stands resolute as three spectral figures whisper destinies into the wind. His ghost will haunt the living.

pt.text: Vinde, espíritos que servis os pensamentos mortais, tirai-me aqui meu sexo.
pt.english: Come, you spirits that tend on mortal thoughts, unsex me here.
pt.back: Come, spirits that serve mortal thoughts, take me here my sex.
pt.controlEnglish: Thou shalt get kings, though thou be none.

pt.text: Uma charneca escocesa enevoada ao crepúsculo. Banquo se mantém firme enquanto três figuras espectrais sussurram destinos ao vento. Seu fantasma há de assombrar os vivos.
pt.english: A misty Scottish heath at twilight. Banquo stands resolute as three spectral figures whisper destinies into the wind. His ghost will haunt the living.
pt.back: A misty Scottish swamp at dusk. Banquo stands firm as three spectral figures whisper destinies to the wind, his ghost haunting the living.
pt.controlEnglish: A windswept Illyrian shore. Viola pulls a sailor's cap over her cropped hair, twin identities shimmering in her eyes. The sea whispers secrets of her lost brother.

pt.text: Gerarás reis, embora não sejas rei.
pt.english: Thou shalt get kings, though thou be none.
pt.back: Thou shalt beget kings, though thou art not a king.
pt.controlEnglish: I am not what I am.

pt.text: Uma costa da Ilíria varrida pelo vento. Viola enterra um gorro de marinheiro sobre o cabelo curto; duas identidades cintilam em seus olhos. O mar sussurra segredos do irmão perdido.
pt.english: A windswept Illyrian shore. Viola pulls a sailor's cap over her cropped hair, twin identities shimmering in her eyes. The sea whispers secrets of her lost brother.
pt.back: A coast of Illyria swept by the wind. Viola buries a sailor’s cap over her short hair; two identities twinkle in her eyes.The sea whispers secrets of the lost brother.
pt.controlEnglish: A sunlit garden in Olivia's estate. Malvolio struts in garish yellow stockings, cross-gartered and grinning, clutching a forged love letter to his chest.

pt.text: Não sou o que sou.
pt.english: I am not what I am.
pt.back: I'm not who I am.
pt.controlEnglish: Some are born great, some achieve greatness, and some have greatness thrust upon them.

pt.text: Um jardim ensolarado na propriedade de Olivia. Malvolio se pavoneia de meias amarelas berrantes com ligas cruzadas, sorridente, apertando contra o peito uma carta de amor forjada.
pt.english: A sunlit garden in Olivia's estate. Malvolio struts in garish yellow stockings, cross-gartered and grinning, clutching a forged love letter to his chest.
pt.back: A sunny garden on Olivia’s estate.Malvolio flaunts in screaming yellow stockings with garters crossed, smiling, squeezing against his chest a forged love letter.
pt.controlEnglish: A veiled countess in mourning lifts her veil to reveal breathtaking beauty. Olivia's garden blooms with jasmine and lavender as the disguised messenger steals her heart.

pt.text: Uns nascem grandes, outros alcançam a grandeza, e a outros a grandeza é imposta.
pt.english: Some are born great, some achieve greatness, and some have greatness thrust upon them.
pt.back: Some are born great, others attain greatness, and to others greatness is imposed.
pt.controlEnglish: Love sought is good, but given unsought, is better.

pt.text: Uma condessa de luto levanta o véu e revela uma beleza de tirar o fôlego. O jardim de Olivia floresce de jasmim e lavanda enquanto o mensageiro disfarçado lhe rouba o coração.
pt.english: A veiled countess in mourning lifts her veil to reveal breathtaking beauty. Olivia's garden blooms with jasmine and lavender as the disguised messenger steals her heart.
pt.back: A mourning countess lifts the veil and reveals a breathtaking beauty.Olivia’s garden blooms with jasmine and lavender as the disguised messenger steals her heart.
pt.controlEnglish: The Roman Senate, marble pillars stained crimson. Brutus stands among the conspirators, his blade still trembling. The weight of the republic rests on his bloodied hands.

pt.text: O amor procurado é bom, mas dado sem ser procurado é melhor.
pt.english: Love sought is good, but given unsought, is better.
pt.back: Love sought is good, but given without being sought is better.
pt.controlEnglish: Not that I loved Caesar less, but that I loved Rome more.

pt.text: O Senado romano, com as colunas de mármore manchadas de carmesim. Bruto está entre os conspiradores, com a lâmina ainda tremendo. O peso da república repousa em suas mãos ensanguentadas.
pt.english: The Roman Senate, marble pillars stained crimson. Brutus stands among the conspirators, his blade still trembling. The weight of the republic rests on his bloodied hands.
pt.back: The Roman Senate, with the marble columns stained with crimson. Brutus is among the conspirators, with his blade still trembling; the weight of the republic rests in his bloody hands.
pt.controlEnglish: A torchlit Roman alley at midnight. Cassius leans close, whispering sedition with a lean and hungry look. Forged letters spill from his toga.

pt.text: Não que eu amasse menos César, mas amava mais Roma.
pt.english: Not that I loved Caesar less, but that I loved Rome more.
pt.back: Not that I loved Caesar less, but I loved Rome more.
pt.controlEnglish: The fault, dear Brutus, is not in our stars, but in ourselves.

pt.text: Uma viela romana à meia-noite, à luz das tochas. Cássio se inclina e sussurra sedição com seu ar magro e faminto. Cartas forjadas caem de sua toga.
pt.english: A torchlit Roman alley at midnight. Cassius leans close, whispering sedition with a lean and hungry look. Forged letters spill from his toga.
pt.back: A Roman alley at midnight, in the light of torches. Cassius leans over and whispers sedition with his skinny, hungry air; forged letters fall from his toga.
pt.controlEnglish: The Roman Forum erupts in fury. Mark Antony holds Caesar's bloodied cloak aloft before the mob, his words turning grief into fire. The republic crumbles with every syllable.

pt.text: A culpa, caro Bruto, não está em nossas estrelas, mas em nós mesmos.
pt.english: The fault, dear Brutus, is not in our stars, but in ourselves.
pt.back: The fault, dear Brutus, is not in our stars but in ourselves.
pt.controlEnglish: Friends, Romans, countrymen, lend me your ears!

pt.text: O Fórum romano irrompe em fúria. Marco Antônio ergue diante da turba o manto ensanguentado de César; suas palavras transformam o luto em fogo. A república desmorona a cada sílaba.
pt.english: The Roman Forum erupts in fury. Mark Antony holds Caesar's bloodied cloak aloft before the mob, his words turning grief into fire. The republic crumbles with every syllable.
pt.back: The Roman Forum bursts out in fury. Marcus Antonius lifts up Caesar's bloody mantle before the crowd; his words turn mourning into fire, and the republic collapses with every syllable.
pt.controlEnglish: The Montague estate at dawn. Lord Montague watches from a high window as his son wanders the misty orchards below, lovesick and unreachable.

pt.text: Amigos, romanos, compatriotas, emprestai-me vossos ouvidos!
pt.english: Friends, Romans, countrymen, lend me your ears!
pt.back: Friends, Romans, compatriots, lend me your ears!
pt.controlEnglish: Many a morning hath he there been seen, with tears augmenting the fresh morning dew.

pt.text: A propriedade dos Montéquio ao amanhecer. O senhor Montéquio observa de uma janela alta o filho que vaga pelos pomares enevoados, doente de amor e inalcançável.
pt.english: The Montague estate at dawn. Lord Montague watches from a high window as his son wanders the misty orchards below, lovesick and unreachable.
pt.back: Mr. Montéquio observes from a high window his son who wanders through the misty orchards, sick of love and unreachable.
pt.controlEnglish: The Capulet great hall draped in silk. Lady Capulet arranges her daughter's fate like flowers in a vase, ambition glittering behind every gracious smile.

pt.text: Muitas manhãs ali foi visto, aumentando com lágrimas o fresco orvalho da manhã.
pt.english: Many a morning hath he there been seen, with tears augmenting the fresh morning dew.
pt.back: Many mornings there was seen, increasing with tears the fresh dew of the morning.
pt.controlEnglish: Marry, that marry is the very theme I came to talk of.

pt.text: Senhor Montéquio
pt.english: Lord Montague
pt.back: Senhor Montéquio
pt.controlEnglish: Lady Capulet

pt.text: O grande salão dos Capuleto, forrado de seda. A senhora Capuleto arranja o destino da filha como flores num vaso; a ambição cintila por trás de cada sorriso gracioso.
pt.english: The Capulet great hall draped in silk. Lady Capulet arranges her daughter's fate like flowers in a vase, ambition glittering behind every gracious smile.
pt.back: Madame Capulet arranges the fate of her daughter like flowers in a vase; ambition sparkles behind every graceful smile, and she is not afraid to put herself at risk.
pt.controlEnglish: The battlements of Elsinore in the cold hour before dawn. Horatio stands vigil beside Hamlet, the one true friend in a court of serpents.

pt.text: Casar: é esse mesmo o assunto de que eu vinha te falar.
pt.english: Marry, that marry is the very theme I came to talk of.
pt.back: Married: this is the very subject of which I came to talk to you.
pt.controlEnglish: Now cracks a noble heart. Good night, sweet prince.

pt.text: Senhora Capuleto
pt.english: Lady Capulet
pt.back: Senhora Capuleto
pt.controlEnglish: Romeo's Ring

pt.text: As ameias de Elsinore na hora fria antes do alvorecer. Horatio vigia ao lado de Hamlet, o único amigo verdadeiro numa corte de serpentes.
pt.english: The battlements of Elsinore in the cold hour before dawn. Horatio stands vigil beside Hamlet, the one true friend in a court of serpents.
pt.back: Horatio watches by the side of Hamlet, the only true friend in a court of serpents.
pt.controlEnglish: A forest clearing aglow with fairy light. Bottom wears an ass's head with bewildered dignity as Titania drapes him in garlands. The fairies stifle their laughter.

pt.text: Agora se parte um nobre coração. Boa noite, doce príncipe.
pt.english: Now cracks a noble heart. Good night, sweet prince.
pt.back: Now a noble heart breaks. Good night, sweet prince.
pt.controlEnglish: I have had a most rare vision. I have had a dream, past the wit of man.

pt.text: Uma clareira da floresta banhada de luz de fadas. Bottom usa uma cabeça de burro com perplexa dignidade enquanto Titania o cobre de guirlandas. As fadas abafam o riso.
pt.english: A forest clearing aglow with fairy light. Bottom wears an ass's head with bewildered dignity as Titania drapes him in garlands. The fairies stifle their laughter.
pt.back: A forest clearing bathed in fairy light. Bottom wears a donkey's head with baffled dignity while Titania covers him with garlands.
pt.controlEnglish: The churchyard of Verona at dusk. Paris lays flowers at Juliet's tomb, unaware of the desperate lover who approaches from the shadows.

pt.text: Tive uma visão raríssima. Tive um sonho que excede o entendimento do homem.
pt.english: I have had a most rare vision. I have had a dream, past the wit of man.
pt.back: I have had a very rare vision. I have had a dream that exceeds the understanding of man.
pt.controlEnglish: These times of woe afford no time to woo.

pt.text: O cemitério de Verona ao anoitecer. Paris deposita flores no túmulo de Julieta, sem saber do amante desesperado que se aproxima vindo das sombras.
pt.english: The churchyard of Verona at dusk. Paris lays flowers at Juliet's tomb, unaware of the desperate lover who approaches from the shadows.
pt.back: Paris lays flowers on Juliet’s grave, unaware of the desperate lover who is approaching from the shadows.
pt.controlEnglish: A pristine beach on Prospero's island. Miranda sees the shipwrecked sailors for the first time, her eyes wide with wonder at a world she never knew existed.

pt.text: Estes tempos de dor não dão tempo para cortejar.
pt.english: These times of woe afford no time to woo.
pt.back: These times of pain give no time for courting.
pt.controlEnglish: O brave new world, that has such people in it!

pt.text: Uma praia intocada na ilha de Próspero. Miranda vê os náufragos pela primeira vez, de olhos arregalados de espanto diante de um mundo que ela não sabia que existia.
pt.english: A pristine beach on Prospero's island. Miranda sees the shipwrecked sailors for the first time, her eyes wide with wonder at a world she never knew existed.
pt.back: Miranda sees the shipwrecked for the first time, with her eyes wide open in amazement at a world that she did not know existed.
pt.controlEnglish: A golden ring rests on a stone balcony ledge, catching moonlight. Inscribed inside is a vow that outlasts death itself. Rose petals spiral around it in an unseen wind.

pt.text: Ó admirável mundo novo, que tem em si tal gente!
pt.english: O brave new world, that has such people in it!
pt.back: O wonderful new world, which has such people in it!
pt.controlEnglish: My bounty is as boundless as the sea, my love as deep.

pt.text: Um anel de ouro repousa no parapeito de pedra de uma sacada e capta o luar. Por dentro, traz gravado um voto que sobrevive à própria morte. Pétalas de rosa rodopiam à sua volta num vento invisível.
pt.english: A golden ring rests on a stone balcony ledge, catching moonlight. Inscribed inside is a vow that outlasts death itself. Rose petals spiral around it in an unseen wind.
pt.back: A golden ring rests on the stone parapet of a balcony and captures the moonlight. Inside, it carries engraved a vow that survives its own death.Rose petals spin around it in an invisible wind.
pt.controlEnglish: Three caskets gleam in a candlelit chamber -- gold, silver, and lead. The lead casket hums with quiet truth, rewarding those wise enough to see past appearances.

pt.text: Minha generosidade é tão ilimitada quanto o mar, meu amor tão profundo.
pt.english: My bounty is as boundless as the sea, my love as deep.
pt.back: My generosity is as boundless as the sea, my love so deep.
pt.controlEnglish: All that glisters is not gold.

pt.text: O anel de Romeu
pt.english: Romeo's Ring
pt.back: The Ring of Romeo
pt.controlEnglish: Portia's Casket

pt.text: Três cofres brilham num aposento à luz de velas: ouro, prata e chumbo. O cofre de chumbo vibra com uma verdade serena e recompensa quem é sábio o bastante para ver além das aparências.
pt.english: Three caskets gleam in a candlelit chamber -- gold, silver, and lead. The lead casket hums with quiet truth, rewarding those wise enough to see past appearances.
pt.back: Three vaults shine in a candlelit chamber: gold, silver and lead.The lead vault vibrates with a serene truth and rewards those who are wise enough to see beyond appearances.
pt.controlEnglish: A tarnished Scottish crown sits on a bloodstained pillow. It pulses with dark ambition, whispering promises of glory to any hand that dares reach for it.

pt.text: Nem tudo o que reluz é ouro.
pt.english: All that glisters is not gold.
pt.back: Not everything that shines is gold.
pt.controlEnglish: Uneasy lies the head that wears a crown.

pt.text: O cofre de Pórcia
pt.english: Portia's Casket
pt.back: The Vault of Porcia
pt.controlEnglish: Macbeth's Crown

pt.text: Uma coroa escocesa embaçada repousa numa almofada manchada de sangue. Pulsa de ambição sombria e sussurra promessas de glória a qualquer mão que ouse se estender para ela.
pt.english: A tarnished Scottish crown sits on a bloodstained pillow. It pulses with dark ambition, whispering promises of glory to any hand that dares reach for it.
pt.back: A hazy Scottish crown rests on a blood-stained pillow, pulsing with dark ambition and whispering promises of glory to any hand that dares reach for it.
pt.controlEnglish: An ancient tome bound in sea-weathered leather floats above a stone altar. Its pages turn by themselves, each one summoning a different storm.

pt.text: Inquieta repousa a cabeça que usa uma coroa.
pt.english: Uneasy lies the head that wears a crown.
pt.back: Restless rests the head that wears a crown.
pt.controlEnglish: I'll drown my book.

pt.text: A coroa de Macbeth
pt.english: Macbeth's Crown
pt.back: The Crown of Macbeth
pt.controlEnglish: The Tempest Codex

pt.text: Um tomo antigo, encadernado em couro curtido pelo mar, flutua sobre um altar de pedra. Suas páginas viram sozinhas, e cada uma invoca uma tempestade diferente.
pt.english: An ancient tome bound in sea-weathered leather floats above a stone altar. Its pages turn by themselves, each one summoning a different storm.
pt.back: An ancient volume, bound in leather tanned by the sea, floats over a stone altar; its pages have turned on their own, and each summons a different storm.
pt.controlEnglish: A crystal vial holds tears that shimmer like captured starlight. Each drop carries the sorrow of a daughter who loved too truly and spoke too plainly.

pt.text: Afogarei meu livro.
pt.english: I'll drown my book.
pt.back: I'll drown my book.
pt.controlEnglish: O dear father, it is thy business that I go about.

pt.text: O códice da tempestade
pt.english: The Tempest Codex
pt.back: The Codex of the Storm
pt.controlEnglish: Cordelia's Tears

pt.text: Um frasco de cristal guarda lágrimas que cintilam como luz de estrelas aprisionada. Cada gota carrega a dor de uma filha que amou com verdade demais e falou com franqueza demais.
pt.english: A crystal vial holds tears that shimmer like captured starlight. Each drop carries the sorrow of a daughter who loved too truly and spoke too plainly.
pt.back: A crystal jar holds tears that sparkle like starlight imprisoned.Each drop carries the pain of a daughter who loved too truly and spoke too frankly.
pt.controlEnglish: A donkey-headed mask hangs from a mossy branch in the fairy wood. Whoever dons it sees the world through enchanted eyes -- and becomes irresistible to fairy queens.

pt.text: Ó querido pai, é de teus assuntos que me ocupo.
pt.english: O dear father, it is thy business that I go about.
pt.back: O dear father, it is your affairs that I am concerned with.
pt.controlEnglish: Bless thee, Bottom! Thou art translated!

pt.text: As lágrimas de Cordélia
pt.english: Cordelia's Tears
pt.back: The tears of Cordelia
pt.controlEnglish: Bottom's Mask

pt.text: Uma máscara com cabeça de burro pende de um galho musgoso no bosque das fadas. Quem a usa vê o mundo com olhos encantados e se torna irresistível para as rainhas das fadas.
pt.english: A donkey-headed mask hangs from a mossy branch in the fairy wood. Whoever dons it sees the world through enchanted eyes -- and becomes irresistible to fairy queens.
pt.back: A donkey-headed mask hangs from a mossy branch in the fairy grove, who wears it sees the world with enchanted eyes and becomes irresistible to fairy queens.
pt.controlEnglish: A gnarled root shaped like a screaming figure is unearthed by candlelight. Soil crumbles away to reveal its twisted, ancient power. The apothecary handles it with trembling reverence.

pt.text: Deus te abençoe, Bottom! Estás transformado!
pt.english: Bless thee, Bottom! Thou art translated!
pt.back: God bless you, Bottom!
pt.controlEnglish: Not poppy, nor mandragora, nor all the drowsy syrups of the world.

pt.text: A máscara de Bottom
pt.english: Bottom's Mask
pt.back: The Mask of Bottom
pt.controlEnglish: Mandrake Root

pt.text: Uma raiz nodosa, com a forma de uma figura que grita, é desenterrada à luz de uma vela. A terra se desfaz e revela seu poder antigo e retorcido. O boticário a segura com trêmula reverência.
pt.english: A gnarled root shaped like a screaming figure is unearthed by candlelight. Soil crumbles away to reveal its twisted, ancient power. The apothecary handles it with trembling reverence.
pt.back: A knotty root, shaped like a screaming figure, is dug up in the light of a candle. The earth disintegrates and reveals its ancient, twisted power, and the pharmacist holds it with trembling reverence.
pt.controlEnglish: A dewdrop clings to a moonlit orchid, glowing with otherworldly violet light. One drop upon sleeping eyelids and the dreamer falls in love with the first creature they see.

pt.text: Nem a papoula, nem a mandrágora, nem todos os xaropes sonolentos do mundo.
pt.english: Not poppy, nor mandragora, nor all the drowsy syrups of the world.
pt.back: Neither the poppy, nor the mandragora, nor all the sleepy syrups in the world.
pt.controlEnglish: Fetch me that flower; the herb I showed thee once.

pt.text: Raiz de mandrágora
pt.english: Mandrake Root
pt.back: Mandragora root
pt.controlEnglish: Oberon's Dew

pt.text: Uma gota de orvalho se prende a uma orquídea ao luar e brilha com uma luz violeta de outro mundo. Uma gota sobre pálpebras adormecidas, e quem sonha se apaixona pela primeira criatura que vir.
pt.english: A dewdrop clings to a moonlit orchid, glowing with otherworldly violet light. One drop upon sleeping eyelids and the dreamer falls in love with the first creature they see.
pt.back: A drop of dew clings to an orchid in the moonlight and shines with a violet light from another world; a drop on sleeping eyelids, and the dreamer falls in love with the first creature he sees.
pt.controlEnglish: A black glass vial weeps green vapor in a darkened corridor. The tincture within has toppled kings and shattered dynasties, one silent drop at a time.

pt.text: Traz-me aquela flor; a erva que uma vez te mostrei.
pt.english: Fetch me that flower; the herb I showed thee once.
pt.back: Bring me that flower; the grass I once showed you.
pt.controlEnglish: In the cauldron boil and bake; eye of newt and toe of frog.

pt.text: Orvalho de Oberon
pt.english: Oberon's Dew
pt.back: Dew of Oberon
pt.controlEnglish: Hemlock Tincture

pt.text: Um frasco de vidro negro exala vapor verde num corredor escuro. A tintura que ele contém derrubou reis e desfez dinastias, uma gota silenciosa de cada vez.
pt.english: A black glass vial weeps green vapor in a darkened corridor. The tincture within has toppled kings and shattered dynasties, one silent drop at a time.
pt.back: A black glass jar exudes green vapor in a dark corridor, the dye it contains has overthrown kings and undone dynasties, one silent drop at a time.
pt.controlEnglish: Pale berries glisten among dark evergreen leaves, harvested under a winter moon. The extract hums with the quiet, persistent magic of the natural world.

pt.text: Tintura de cicuta
pt.english: Hemlock Tincture
pt.back: Tincture of cicuta
pt.controlEnglish: Mistletoe Extract

pt.text: Bagas pálidas reluzem entre escuras folhas perenes, colhidas sob uma lua de inverno. O extrato vibra com a magia serena e persistente do mundo natural.
pt.english: Pale berries glisten among dark evergreen leaves, harvested under a winter moon. The extract hums with the quiet, persistent magic of the natural world.
pt.back: Pale berries gleam among dark evergreen leaves, harvested under a winter moon.The extract vibrates with the serene and persistent magic of the natural world.
pt.controlEnglish: A pearl-stoppered flask holds luminous blue liquid that shifts like a living sea. Within it, tiny coral formations grow and dissolve. It smells of salt and forgotten voyages.

pt.text: No caldeirão fervei e cozei; olho de salamandra e dedo de rã.
pt.english: In the cauldron boil and bake; eye of newt and toe of frog.
pt.back: In the cauldron I boiled and cooked; salamander eye and frog finger.
pt.controlEnglish: Full fathom five thy father lies; of his bones are coral made.

pt.text: Extrato de visco
pt.english: Mistletoe Extract
pt.back: Mistletoe extract
pt.controlEnglish: Mermaid's Tears

pt.text: Um frasco com rolha de pérola guarda um líquido azul luminoso que se move como um mar vivo. Lá dentro, minúsculas formações de coral crescem e se desfazem. Tem cheiro de sal e de viagens esquecidas.
pt.english: A pearl-stoppered flask holds luminous blue liquid that shifts like a living sea. Within it, tiny coral formations grow and dissolve. It smells of salt and forgotten voyages.
pt.back: A bottle with a pearl stopper holds a luminous blue liquid that moves like a living sea. Inside, tiny coral formations grow and fall apart.It smells of salt and forgotten travels.
pt.controlEnglish: A dusty apothecary shop in Mantua's poorest quarter. A desperate elixir glows amber in a cracked vial, potent enough to bridge the gap between life and death.

pt.text: A cinco braças jaz teu pai; de seus ossos se fez coral.
pt.english: Full fathom five thy father lies; of his bones are coral made.
pt.back: At five arms lies thy father; of his bones is made coral.
pt.controlEnglish: Put this in any liquid thing you will, and drink it off; and, if you had the strength of twenty men, it would dispatch you straight.

pt.text: Lágrimas de sereia
pt.english: Mermaid's Tears
pt.back: Tears of mermaid
pt.controlEnglish: Apothecary's Elixir

pt.text: Uma botica empoeirada no bairro mais pobre de Mântua. Um elixir de desespero brilha, cor de âmbar, num frasco rachado, potente o bastante para transpor o intervalo entre a vida e a morte.
pt.english: A dusty apothecary shop in Mantua's poorest quarter. A desperate elixir glows amber in a cracked vial, potent enough to bridge the gap between life and death.
pt.back: A dusty pharmacy in the poorest neighborhood of Mantua. An elixir of despair shines, amber-colored, in a cracked vial, powerful enough to bridge the gap between life and death.
pt.controlEnglish: A carpet of golden daffodils stretches along the shores of a still lake. Wordsworth walks among them, notebook in hand, the Cumberland fells rising behind him.

pt.text: Põe isto em qualquer líquido que quiseres e bebe; e, ainda que tivesses a força de vinte homens, isto te despacharia num instante.
pt.english: Put this in any liquid thing you will, and drink it off; and, if you had the strength of twenty men, it would dispatch you straight.
pt.back: Put this in any liquid you like and drink; and even if you had the strength of twenty men, it would deliver you in an instant.
pt.controlEnglish: I wandered lonely as a cloud that floats on high o'er vales and hills.

pt.text: Elixir do boticário
pt.english: Apothecary's Elixir
pt.back: Elixir of the pharmacist
pt.controlEnglish: Yorick's Skull

pt.text: Um tapete de narcisos dourados se estende pelas margens de um lago parado. Wordsworth caminha entre eles, de caderno na mão, com os montes de Cumberland se erguendo atrás de si.
pt.english: A carpet of golden daffodils stretches along the shores of a still lake. Wordsworth walks among them, notebook in hand, the Cumberland fells rising behind him.
pt.back: A carpet of golden daffodils stretches along the shores of a still lake, and Wordsworth walks among them with his notebook in hand, the hills of Cumberland rising behind him.
pt.controlEnglish: A becalmed ship drifts on a painted ocean. The Ancient Mariner stares at the albatross around his neck as spectral figures rise from the glassy sea.

pt.text: Eu vagava solitário como uma nuvem que flutua bem alto sobre vales e colinas.
pt.english: I wandered lonely as a cloud that floats on high o'er vales and hills.
pt.back: I wandered lonely like a cloud that floats high over valleys and hills.
pt.controlEnglish: Water, water, every where, nor any drop to drink.

pt.text: Um navio em calmaria deriva num oceano pintado. O velho marinheiro fita o albatroz que traz pendurado ao pescoço enquanto figuras espectrais sobem do mar vítreo.
pt.english: A becalmed ship drifts on a painted ocean. The Ancient Mariner stares at the albatross around his neck as spectral figures rise from the glassy sea.
pt.back: A calm ship drifts in a painted ocean, the old sailor hanging his albatross around his neck as spectral figures rise from the glassy sea.
pt.controlEnglish: A Hampstead garden in autumn. Keats sits beneath a plum tree, writing feverishly as a nightingale sings from the darkening branches above.

pt.text: Água, água por toda parte, e nem uma gota para beber.
pt.english: Water, water, every where, nor any drop to drink.
pt.back: Water, water everywhere, and not a drop to drink.
pt.controlEnglish: A thing of beauty is a joy for ever: its loveliness increases.

pt.text: Um jardim de Hampstead no outono. Keats, sentado debaixo de uma ameixeira, escreve febrilmente enquanto um rouxinol canta nos galhos que escurecem.
pt.english: A Hampstead garden in autumn. Keats sits beneath a plum tree, writing feverishly as a nightingale sings from the darkening branches above.
pt.back: A Hampstead garden in autumn: Keats, sitting under a plum tree, writes feverishly while a nightingale sings on the darkening branches.
pt.controlEnglish: A Venetian palazzo at midnight. Byron stands on the balcony, cape billowing, gazing across the dark canal. A half-finished manuscript burns in the fireplace behind him.

pt.text: Uma coisa bela é uma alegria para sempre: seu encanto cresce.
pt.english: A thing of beauty is a joy for ever: its loveliness increases.
pt.back: A beautiful thing is a joy forever: its charm grows.
pt.controlEnglish: She walks in beauty, like the night of cloudless climes and starry skies.

pt.text: Um palácio veneziano à meia-noite. Byron está na sacada, com a capa ao vento, olhando o canal escuro. Atrás dele, um manuscrito inacabado arde na lareira.
pt.english: A Venetian palazzo at midnight. Byron stands on the balcony, cape billowing, gazing across the dark canal. A half-finished manuscript burns in the fireplace behind him.
pt.back: A Venetian palace at midnight. Byron is on the balcony, with his cloak in the wind, looking out over the dark canal, and behind him an unfinished manuscript burning in the fireplace.
pt.controlEnglish: A candlelit study in Geneva during a thunderstorm. Mary writes by lightning flash as the creature stirs in the shadows behind her. Science and horror become one.

pt.text: Ela caminha em beleza, como a noite de climas sem nuvens e céus estrelados.
pt.english: She walks in beauty, like the night of cloudless climes and starry skies.
pt.back: She walks in beauty, like the night of cloudless climates and starry skies.
pt.controlEnglish: Beware; for I am fearless, and therefore powerful.

pt.text: Um gabinete à luz de velas em Genebra, durante uma trovoada. Mary escreve ao clarão dos relâmpagos enquanto a criatura se mexe nas sombras atrás dela. Ciência e horror se tornam um só.
pt.english: A candlelit study in Geneva during a thunderstorm. Mary writes by lightning flash as the creature stirs in the shadows behind her. Science and horror become one.
pt.back: A candlelit office in Geneva, during a thunderstorm. Mary writes in the light of lightning while the creature moves in the shadows behind her.Science and horror become one.
pt.controlEnglish: A dim chamber lit by a dying fire. Poe sits hunched at his desk as a raven alights on the bust of Pallas. The word "Nevermore" echoes in the shadows.

pt.text: Cuidado; pois não tenho medo, e por isso sou poderoso.
pt.english: Beware; for I am fearless, and therefore powerful.
pt.back: Beware; for I am not afraid, and therefore I am mighty.
pt.controlEnglish: To see a World in a Grain of Sand and a Heaven in a Wild Flower.

pt.text: Um aposento sombrio iluminado por um fogo que se apaga. Poe está curvado sobre a escrivaninha quando um corvo pousa no busto de Palas. A palavra “Nunca mais” ecoa nas sombras.
pt.english: A dim chamber lit by a dying fire. Poe sits hunched at his desk as a raven alights on the bust of Pallas. The word "Nevermore" echoes in the shadows.
pt.back: A dark room lit by a fire that goes out. Poe is bent over the desk when a crow lands on Palas’ bust, and the word “Never Again” echoes in the shadows.
pt.controlEnglish: A London printing workshop ablaze with visionary light. Blake etches a tiger into copper as the beast materializes from the plate, burning bright in the forests of the night.

pt.text: Uma oficina de impressão em Londres, incendiada de luz visionária. Blake grava um tigre no cobre enquanto a fera se materializa da chapa, ardendo brilhante nas florestas da noite.
pt.english: A London printing workshop ablaze with visionary light. Blake etches a tiger into copper as the beast materializes from the plate, burning bright in the forests of the night.
pt.back: A printing shop in London, burned with visionary light.Blake engraves a tiger on copper as the beast materializes from the plate, burning brightly in the forests of night.
pt.controlEnglish: A windswept Italian clifftop. Shelley faces the storm, arms wide, as the west wind tears pages from his notebook and scatters them across the Mediterranean.

pt.text: Ver um mundo num grão de areia e um céu numa flor silvestre.
pt.english: To see a World in a Grain of Sand and a Heaven in a Wild Flower.
pt.back: See a world in a grain of sand and a sky in a wild flower.
pt.controlEnglish: If Winter comes, can Spring be far behind?

pt.text: O alto de um penhasco italiano varrido pelo vento. Shelley enfrenta a tempestade de braços abertos, enquanto o vento oeste arranca páginas de seu caderno e as espalha pelo Mediterrâneo.
pt.english: A windswept Italian clifftop. Shelley faces the storm, arms wide, as the west wind tears pages from his notebook and scatters them across the Mediterranean.
pt.back: On top of an Italian cliff swept by the wind, Shelley faces the storm with open arms as the west wind tears pages from her notebook and scatters them across the Mediterranean.
pt.controlEnglish: A sunlit room in Florence. Elizabeth writes at a window overlooking the Arno, her spaniel at her feet. Love letters from Robert lie open on the desk.

pt.text: Se o inverno chega, pode a primavera estar longe?
pt.english: If Winter comes, can Spring be far behind?
pt.back: If winter comes, can spring be far away?
pt.controlEnglish: How do I love thee? Let me count the ways.

pt.text: Um quarto cheio de sol em Florença. Elizabeth escreve junto a uma janela com vista para o Arno, com seu spaniel aos pés. As cartas de amor de Robert estão abertas sobre a escrivaninha.
pt.english: A sunlit room in Florence. Elizabeth writes at a window overlooking the Arno, her spaniel at her feet. Love letters from Robert lie open on the desk.
pt.back: A sunny room in Florence. Elizabeth is writing by a window overlooking the Arno, with her spaniel at her feet, and Robert’s love letters are open on the desk.
pt.controlEnglish: A Pre-Raphaelite garden in fading autumn light. Christina sits among fallen leaves, composing verses that ache with beauty and quiet resignation.

pt.text: Como te amo? Deixa-me contar as maneiras.
pt.english: How do I love thee? Let me count the ways.
pt.back: How do I love you? Let me tell the ways.
pt.controlEnglish: Remember me when I am gone away, gone far away into the silent land.

pt.text: Um jardim pré-rafaelita na luz minguante do outono. Christina está sentada entre folhas caídas, compondo versos que doem de beleza e de serena resignação.
pt.english: A Pre-Raphaelite garden in fading autumn light. Christina sits among fallen leaves, composing verses that ache with beauty and quiet resignation.
pt.back: A pre-Raphaelite garden in the waning light of autumn, Christina sits among fallen leaves, composing verses that give of beauty and serene resignation.
pt.controlEnglish: Mount Olympus splits the sky. Zeus sits on a throne of clouds, lightning arcing between his fingers. Below, the mortal world trembles at his gaze.

pt.text: Lembra-te de mim quando eu tiver partido, partido para longe, para a terra silenciosa.
pt.english: Remember me when I am gone away, gone far away into the silent land.
pt.back: Remember me when I'm gone, gone far away to the silent land.
pt.controlEnglish: I am the cloud-gatherer, lord of the wide heavens.

pt.text: O monte Olimpo rasga o céu. Zeus está sentado num trono de nuvens, com o relâmpago saltando entre os dedos. Lá embaixo, o mundo mortal treme sob seu olhar.
pt.english: Mount Olympus splits the sky. Zeus sits on a throne of clouds, lightning arcing between his fingers. Below, the mortal world trembles at his gaze.
pt.back: Mount Olympus rips the sky apart. Zeus sits on a throne of clouds, with lightning leaping between his fingers, and beneath him the mortal world trembles under his gaze.
pt.controlEnglish: The Parthenon gleams in golden light. Athena stands in full armor, her owl perched on her shield, her grey eyes seeing through every mortal deception.

pt.text: Sou o que ajunta as nuvens, senhor dos vastos céus.
pt.english: I am the cloud-gatherer, lord of the wide heavens.
pt.back: I am the one who gathers the clouds, Lord of the vast heavens.
pt.controlEnglish: The owl of wisdom takes flight only at dusk.

pt.text: O Partenon resplandece numa luz dourada. Atena está de pé, com a armadura completa, a coruja pousada no escudo, os olhos cinzentos enxergando além de todo engano mortal.
pt.english: The Parthenon gleams in golden light. Athena stands in full armor, her owl perched on her shield, her grey eyes seeing through every mortal deception.
pt.back: The Parthenon shines in a golden light, Athena is standing in full armor, the owl resting on the shield, her gray eyes seeing beyond all mortal deception.
pt.controlEnglish: A golden chariot races across the dawn sky. Apollo plays his lyre as sunlight pours from the wheels, painting the world in color.

pt.text: A coruja da sabedoria só levanta voo ao anoitecer.
pt.english: The owl of wisdom takes flight only at dusk.
pt.back: The owl of wisdom only takes flight at dusk.
pt.controlEnglish: I am the god of song, of healing, and of the radiant sun.

pt.text: Uma carruagem de ouro corre pelo céu da alvorada. Apolo toca a lira enquanto a luz do sol jorra das rodas e pinta o mundo de cor.
pt.english: A golden chariot races across the dawn sky. Apollo plays his lyre as sunlight pours from the wheels, painting the world in color.
pt.back: A golden chariot runs through the dawn sky, Apollo plays his lyre as sunlight gushes from the wheels and paints the world in colour.
pt.controlEnglish: The shores of Cyprus at dawn. Aphrodite rises from sea foam, doves circling above as waves lay pearls at her feet. The world holds its breath.

pt.text: Sou o deus do canto, da cura e do sol radiante.
pt.english: I am the god of song, of healing, and of the radiant sun.
pt.back: I am the god of singing, healing and the radiant sun.
pt.controlEnglish: Even the gods cannot resist the power of love.

pt.text: As praias de Chipre ao amanhecer. Afrodite surge da espuma do mar; pombas voam em círculos e as ondas depositam pérolas a seus pés. O mundo prende a respiração.
pt.english: The shores of Cyprus at dawn. Aphrodite rises from sea foam, doves circling above as waves lay pearls at her feet. The world holds its breath.
pt.back: The beaches of Cyprus at dawn. Aphrodite rises from the foam of the sea; doves fly in circles and the waves deposit pearls at her feet.
pt.controlEnglish: A blur of winged sandals across the sky. Hermes weaves between thunderbolts, a divine message clutched in one hand and a thief's grin on his face.

pt.text: Nem os deuses conseguem resistir ao poder do amor.
pt.english: Even the gods cannot resist the power of love.
pt.back: Not even the gods can resist the power of love.
pt.controlEnglish: Swift as thought, I carry the words of gods to mortal ears.

pt.text: Um vulto de sandálias aladas atravessa o céu. Hermes serpenteia por entre os raios, com uma mensagem divina apertada numa mão e um sorriso de ladrão no rosto.
pt.english: A blur of winged sandals across the sky. Hermes weaves between thunderbolts, a divine message clutched in one hand and a thief's grin on his face.
pt.back: Hermes winds through the rays, holding a divine message in one hand and a thief's smile on his face, while a crowd of winged sandals crosses the sky.
pt.controlEnglish: The throne room of the Underworld, lit by rivers of pale fire. Hades sits with Cerberus at his feet, his helm of darkness on the armrest. The dead file past in endless silence.

pt.text: Veloz como o pensamento, levo as palavras dos deuses a ouvidos mortais.
pt.english: Swift as thought, I carry the words of gods to mortal ears.
pt.back: Fast as thought, I carry the words of the gods to mortal ears.
pt.controlEnglish: All souls come to me in the end. I am patient.

pt.text: A sala do trono do Submundo, iluminada por rios de fogo pálido. Hades está sentado com Cérbero a seus pés e o elmo das trevas no braço do trono. Os mortos desfilam num silêncio sem fim.
pt.english: The throne room of the Underworld, lit by rivers of pale fire. Hades sits with Cerberus at his feet, his helm of darkness on the armrest. The dead file past in endless silence.
pt.back: The throne room of the Underworld, lit by rivers of pale fire. Hades sits with Cerberus at his feet and the helmet of darkness on the arm of the throne.The dead march in endless silence.
pt.controlEnglish: A throne split between spring and shadow. Persephone holds a pomegranate in one hand and a crown of flowers in the other, queen of two realms.

pt.text: Todas as almas vêm a mim no fim. Sou paciente.
pt.english: All souls come to me in the end. I am patient.
pt.back: All souls come to me in the end. I am patient.
pt.controlEnglish: Six seeds I ate, and bound myself between two worlds forever.

pt.text: Um trono dividido entre a primavera e a sombra. Perséfone segura uma romã numa mão e uma coroa de flores na outra, rainha de dois reinos.
pt.english: A throne split between spring and shadow. Persephone holds a pomegranate in one hand and a crown of flowers in the other, queen of two realms.
pt.back: A throne divided between spring and shadow, Persephone holding a pomegranate in one hand and a crown of flowers in the other, queen of two kingdoms.
pt.controlEnglish: A storm-battered ship rounds a rocky headland. Odysseus lashes himself to the mast as the Sirens sing from the cliffs. His eyes burn with the memory of Ithaca.

pt.text: Seis sementes comi, e prendi-me para sempre entre dois mundos.
pt.english: Six seeds I ate, and bound myself between two worlds forever.
pt.back: I ate six seeds, and I was trapped forever between two worlds.
pt.controlEnglish: Tell me, O Muse, of the man of many ways, who wandered far.

pt.text: Um navio castigado pela tempestade contorna um cabo rochoso. Odisseu se amarra ao mastro enquanto as sereias cantam dos penhascos. Em seus olhos arde a lembrança de Ítaca.
pt.english: A storm-battered ship rounds a rocky headland. Odysseus lashes himself to the mast as the Sirens sing from the cliffs. His eyes burn with the memory of Ithaca.
pt.back: A storm-stricken ship circles a rocky cape. Odysseus binds himself to the mast as the sirens sing from the cliffs, and in his eyes burns the memory of Ithaca.
pt.controlEnglish: A ruined temple at the edge of the world. Medusa turns, her serpent hair hissing. Stone warriors litter the floor, frozen in their final charge.

pt.text: Fala-me, ó Musa, do homem de muitos caminhos, que vagou para longe.
pt.english: Tell me, O Muse, of the man of many ways, who wandered far.
pt.back: Tell me, O Moses, of the man of many ways, who wandered far away.
pt.controlEnglish: Look upon me, if you dare. My gaze is the last thing you will see.

pt.text: Um templo em ruínas na borda do mundo. Medusa se vira, com a cabeleira de serpentes sibilando. Guerreiros de pedra cobrem o chão, imobilizados em sua última investida.
pt.english: A ruined temple at the edge of the world. Medusa turns, her serpent hair hissing. Stone warriors litter the floor, frozen in their final charge.
pt.back: A temple in ruins at the edge of the world. Medusa turns around, her snake-haired hair wheezing, and stone warriors cover the ground, immobilized on their last assault.
pt.controlEnglish: The plains of Troy at dawn. Achilles charges in blazing armor, his war cry splitting the air. Behind him, Greek ships burn on the shore.

pt.text: Olha para mim, se te atreves. Meu olhar é a última coisa que verás.
pt.english: Look upon me, if you dare. My gaze is the last thing you will see.
pt.back: Look at me, if you dare. My look is the last thing you'll see.
pt.controlEnglish: I would rather live a short life of glory than a long life forgotten.

pt.text: As planícies de Troia ao amanhecer. Aquiles avança numa armadura flamejante, e seu grito de guerra rasga o ar. Atrás dele, as naus gregas ardem na praia.
pt.english: The plains of Troy at dawn. Achilles charges in blazing armor, his war cry splitting the air. Behind him, Greek ships burn on the shore.
pt.back: The plains of Troy at dawn. Achilles advances in flaming armor, and his cry of war tears the air.Behind him, the Greek ships burn on the beach.
pt.controlEnglish: A grand stage materializes. The Sonnet Man steps forward from a golden spotlight, microphone in hand. Shakespeare's words transform into hip-hop bars as the crowd cheers.

pt.text: Prefiro viver uma vida curta de glória a uma vida longa esquecida.
pt.english: I would rather live a short life of glory than a long life forgotten.
pt.back: I would rather live a short life of glory than a long forgotten life.
pt.controlEnglish: Shall I compare thee to a summer's day?
